cuda: expert paging with a direct-mapped residency cache

With the address table in place, an expert stack can live in pinned host memory
and be read per expert instead of having to fit in VRAM. This adds the landing
slots and the policy that decides what goes in them.

Per expert tensor: a slab of n_slots expert-sized slots, plus residency
bookkeeping that stays on the device so the policy runs inside the graph rather
than forcing a readback, which a capture would not allow. Each decode probes the
routed experts against the slots, awards a slot to each miss, copies those
experts in, and repoints the table entries at the slots. Hits read from the slot
they already occupy; anything that loses a slot contest reads in place from host
memory, which is correct if slower.

The probe reserves a slot it hits with an atomicMin, so a miss mapping to the
same slot cannot claim it and overwrite the contents mid-call. Without that
reservation a hit and a miss can collide and the hit reads the wrong expert,
which shows up as fluent output that is quietly wrong rather than as a crash.

Paging is skipped for a tensor already resident in VRAM: copying a resident
expert into a slot spends bandwidth and VRAM for nothing. The residency query
runs once per tensor via the pointer attributes.

Opt-in through GGML_MOE_PAGE_IN, with GGML_MOE_PAGE_SLOTS sizing the pool.
Requires the address table, since paging works by repointing entries.

vulkan: hoist dequantize4 loads for turbo2/3/4 KV dequant

dequantize4() called dequantize() twice, each re-reading .qs[] (and
.signs[] for turbo3) independently. With iqs%4==0 (guaranteed by every
caller), elements iqs..iqs+3 share a single qs byte (4 per byte for
turbo2/3, 2 consecutive bytes for turbo4's nibble-packed layout) and,
for turbo3, a single signs byte (iqs/8 constant over the range). One
load of each is enough instead of two (turbo2/3) or four (turbo4).

qs/signs byte patterns per type, bit-exact match) and compiles clean
with glslc for the two consumers of dequantize4() in this file
(copy_from_quant.comp, get_rows_quant.comp).

cuda: make the mul_mat bias, residual and GLU epilogue fusions observable

test_mul_mat_residual_fusion had no required_fusion() at all, so the ADD epilogue it exists
to cover was unobservable: a regression that kept the arithmetic correct passed silently.
test_mul_mat_vec_fusion had the same gap for the GLU epilogue.

Add two counters next to the existing ones and increment them where the epilogues are
actually dispatched (six GLU sites, three bias sites), then require them from the tests.
A residual is a full same-shape operand arriving as fusion x_bias, so it shares the
mul_mat_bias counter with a broadcast bias.

The residual guard is gated to what was measured on CDNA2 rather than to what looked
plausible: the epilogue folds in only on the single-column vector path, and never when the
residual aliases the product, which the dispatch declines rather than read back what it has
written. Requiring it unconditionally fails 21 of 24 cases on a correct build. That gate may
differ on other architectures, the same way the SHARED_SRC1 bound needed narrowing for the
CDNA1 mmvq crossover, so it is deliberately conservative.

Verified the guards can fail, not just pass: with a deliberately wrong counter name both
suites report unknown fusion counter and go 0/24 and 0/360. With the real names,
MUL_MAT_RESIDUAL_FUSION 24/24, MUL_MAT_VEC_FUSION 360/360, and the neighbouring suites are
unchanged (MUL_MAT_SHARED_SRC1 12/12, ELEM_CHAIN_FUSION 5/5, MUL_MAT_ID_REDUCE 6/6).

cuda: count mul_mat_bias only when the scale fusion carries a bias

The scale fusion site in ggml_cuda_try_fuse folds a lane scale with an
optional bias. Incrementing mul_mat_bias unconditionally there counted
scale-only fusions as ADD epilogues, so a required_fusion("mul_mat_bias")
guard could be satisfied by a fusion that folded no bias at all.

cuda: try the bias form of the mul_mat + scale fusion first

The scale-only op list (MUL_MAT, MUL) is a prefix of the bias form
(MUL_MAT, MUL, ADD), and the loop tried it first. Whenever a bias ADD
followed, the 2-op fusion matched and the ADD ran as a separate kernel,
so the with_bias branch never fired. Same for the MUL_MAT_ID form.

The mmvq epilogue applies the scale before the bias, so folding the ADD
computes the same (x * scale) + bias.

(previous work in this area had no real model to test against), found
a large, real correctness regression: mean KLD 0.07 (max 4.3) between
streaming and non-streaming output, versus ~0.000000 for every other
architecture validated this way (turbo, iSWA). The initial hypothesis
was a bug in the K-only page-geometry special-case added earlier this
branch (ggml_cuda_kv_stream_page_bytes()'s head_dim_v==0 handling):

called with k_all passed as both K and V) always needs a real V-shaped

doesn't consume V".

special-casing entirely (both in fattn.cu and its two call sites) and
re-ran the same KL-divergence comparison. Result was bit-identical

benefit, and re-excluded LLM_ARCH_DEEPSEEK4 in the architecture

DSV4's online-compression bookkeeping (comp_plan's state_pos/
state_persist_*/state_snapshot_* row addressing) not surviving the

cuda: remove two always-on kv-stream costs from the flag-off path

ggml_cuda_graph_update_required scanned every node and every src of every
node (up to GGML_MAX_SRC) for a live KV streaming runtime on every graph
compute - including every decode step - before the cheap cgraph->uid
early-out that lets CUDA graph replay skip almost everything. Paid by
every user regardless of whether streaming is in use at all.

Add a process-wide live-runtime counter (incremented/decremented exactly
at real construction/destruction, not at reference-count retain/release)
and skip the scan entirely when it's zero. Sound because a live tensor
can only reference a runtime through its buffer, which itself holds a
reference to that runtime - so once the global count is zero, no live
tensor anywhere can reference one, and the scan would find generation 0
regardless.

cuda: guard the zero-normalizer divide in kv_stream_normalize_chunk_results

kv_stream_normalize_chunk_results divided every row's chunked-attention
accumulator by its softmax normalizer unconditionally. A row whose mask
is entirely -inf (a padding row that rounds the launch grid out to a

streamed attention kernel's transient workspace

mode: an arena that constructs fine can still hit a hard, unrecoverable

reduction workspace (four small buffers: parts/meta/accumulator/
accumulator_meta). That workspace draws from the device's general CUDA
memory pool (ctx.pool()), not from the arena itself, so a well-sized
arena and a tight VRAM margin can still combine into a mid-request
abort that takes down an already-serving process.

worst case those four allocations can reach from the model's query

and the MMA-prefill path, which scales with the real ubatch token
count but uses only one partial). llama_context construction now calls

ggml_backend_dev_memory(), and refuses construction with a clear,
actionable error if reserving the arena wouldn't leave that much
headroom - the same clean, caught failure category as an oversized
arena, instead of ever reaching the unsafe one.

This uses free VRAM as measured at that point in construction; later
allocations (e.g. the compute buffer) aren't yet accounted for, so it
catches the clearly-too-tight case, not a formal guarantee - documented
as such in docs/kv-stream.md.

kv-cache: refuse state save/load while block KV streaming is active

state_write_data/state_read_data (and their _meta counterparts) read
and write each layer's K/V tensor via a flat byte offset into
cell-position order (io.write_tensor(k, range.first*k_size_row,
buf_size)). That's only correct when the tensor's own buffer actually
holds every cell contiguously in that order, which is true for an
ordinary KV buffer but not for a block-streamed one: only a resident
subset of pages lives in the buffer kv_stream_adapt() last synced, and
the authoritative copy of the rest lives in host RAM behind the
streaming runtime. Saving state this way would silently write whatever
happened to be resident, not the real KV content, and produce a state
file that looks valid and isn't - untested and unrefused before this.

Refuse cleanly in state_write/state_read_sinfo when kv_stream_runtime
is active, matching how streaming already refuses other unsupported
combinations (single-sequence, --swa-full) rather than support+test a
combination nothing in this branch validates. seq_rm/seq_cp are left
untouched - they're pure cell-metadata bookkeeping that doesn't touch
K/V tensor content and are core to how the server manages context
(e.g. n_discard) even under streaming, so refusing them would break
normal operation for a much smaller and more speculative risk than the
state save/load path's demonstrated one.

Verified against the real local Qwen3.8-27B-AD model via the server's
/slots/{id}?action=save endpoint: with streaming on, the save now fails
cleanly with this error and the server keeps serving; with streaming
off, the same endpoint still saves a full, real state file (157 MB)
exactly as before. test-save-load-state also still passes.

docs/kv-stream: document that streamed output isn't bit-identical

Two intentional design choices mean streamed output is close to
non-streamed, not exactly equal, and can even vary run-to-run:

- The chunked reduction's sequential online-softmax rescale sums the
  same terms in a different order than ordinary Flash Attention's
  single combined pass (flash_attn_combine_results) - floating-point
  addition isn't associative, so this is a real (tiny) numerical
  difference, already reflected in every correctness check this PR
  ran (mean KLD ~0.000000, 99%+ same-top-token, not exact equality).
- The span tuner picks between the coalesced and bounded-span streamed
  kernels by comparing wall-clock timing across trial runs, so which
  one wins - and therefore the exact numerical result within that
  tolerance - depends on transient timing noise and can differ between
  runs of the same request.

Neither was previously stated in the docs.

kv-stream: allow seq_rm, so the server and CLI can run with an arena

llama_kv_cache::seq_rm threw unconditionally while streaming, which made
--kv-stream-arena-mib unusable outside llama-perplexity: the server calls
seq_rm on the first task through prompt_clear(), and common_context_can_seq_rm
probes it during startup, so every request died with

  got exception: seq_rm is not supported while block KV streaming is active

Returning false instead is not an option either - common_context_seq_rm
turns a false into GGML_ABORT.

seq_rm is safe here. It only edits cell bookkeeping: which positions and
sequence ids a slot holds. No K/V bytes move, so the host cache stays
authoritative and the resident GPU mirror stays valid. A freed slot is not
attended again until some later ubatch writes it through set_rows, which
marks the row dirty and refreshes the mirror exactly as it does for a slot
that was never used. seq_cp and seq_add (K-shift) keep refusing: the first
aliases one slot into a second sequence, the second rewrites K in place on
the GPU.

Also stop the server from retrying prompt-cache saves on a context that
cannot serialize its KV cache. State saving is still refused under
streaming by design, and prompt_save was calling into it on every request,
logging two errors each time and spending a cache slot on an entry

kv-stream: warn when the F16 fallback is active, and document its real cost

A build without GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS (the default) compiles out the
direct_attention branch of get_attention_mode entirely, so every streamed
K/V pair falls back to dequantizing each page to F16 on every ubatch. That
cost scales with the KV already in the cache, so prefill goes from flat to
roughly O(n^1.7) the moment an arena is enabled - it is not the fixed
factor docs/kv-stream.md described.

-c 65536 -b 2048 -ub 512, identical prompts and flags in both builds,
prefill t/s at arena 1024 MiB:

  tokens   flag on   flag off
    3902      3293       1743
   11193      3336        975
   17490      3171        700
   39511      2810        352

Arena off is flat near 2900-3300 t/s in both builds, so with the flag on
streaming costs 4-6% at 40K tokens and without it the same run is 8x
slower than its own baseline, widening with context. Arena size is not the
variable: 4096 MiB lands within 3% of 1024 MiB at every length in both
builds.

gets benchmarked by mistake and read as the feature being slow. Add a
type_pair_direct proc address alongside the existing type_pair_supported,
and have llama_kv_cache log one warning naming the K/V pair that fell back
and the flag to rebuild with. Update the docs section with the table above.

docs/kv-stream: document MTP interaction, with measurements

Nothing said how speculative decoding and block KV streaming compose, and
the question came up: does the arena take the draft cache too, and does
streaming cost MTP its speedup? Neither, as it turns out, but it was only
knowable by reading common/speculative.cpp.

State it plainly: the draft context is forced to kv_stream_arena_mib = 0, so
the MTP draft KV cache stays in ordinary VRAM and only the target streams,
and rejected draft tokens roll back through seq_rm, which is bookkeeping-only
and safe under streaming.

Add the numbers behind that, measured on an RTX 5090 with Qwen3.8-27B-Q5_0
plus its Q4_0 MTP draft, two repetitions per cell. The arena is free while
the working set is resident and costs 3-4% once pages genuinely stream; MTP
is worth 1.6x at short context, 1.87x at a 9748-token prompt that still fits
resident, and 1.28x with the cache actively streaming. Draft and accept
counts are identical with and without the arena at a given context, so the
draft path itself is untouched.

Also record a sharper symptom of the phase-classification gap already
documented below: under real streaming pressure the MTP request collects
zero decode deadline samples and holds 22 resident pages/layer where the
same request without MTP collects 26 samples and settles at 31. The
partition controller never adapts because a verification batch is never
classified as generation. It costs throughput MTP could have had; it does
not cause a regression.

XOR mask via arithmetic: 3 - 3*sign_bit (no ternary)
Sign via arithmetic: 2*sign_bit - 1 (no ternary)
Magnitude via FMA chain: fma(b0*b1, D3, fma(b1, D2, fma(b0, D1, M0)))

perf: parallel k_set_rows_turbo3 + optimise KQ/V dequant — +31% decode (71→94 t/s, 98.5% of F16)

    turbo3 block — load qs/signs once instead of twice per pair

    signs byte for all 4 elements; unrolled float2 / half2 output pairs

fix: VEC flash-attn Q/K stride mismatch in vec_dot_fattn_vec_KQ_turbo3_0

The outer loop in vec_dot_fattn_vec_KQ_turbo3_0 stepped k_KQ_0 by
`nthreads` (8), but the Q register file is loaded in blocks of
`nthreads*cpy_ne` (32) elements per thread — the same pattern used by
the f16/bf16 VEC kernels. This caused thread t>0 to pair K element
(16s + 2t) against Q element (64*(s/4) + 8t + 2*(s%4)), a complete
index mismatch. Every generated token had garbage attention scores.

Fix: match the f16 kernel pattern — step by nthreads*cpy_ne, add an
inner k_KQ_1 loop over cpy_ne pairs, and index Q_v as
Q_v[k_KQ_0/nthreads + k_KQ_1].

that documented the symptom of this bug.

perf: V12 single-phase fused TQ mmvq — shmem activation, no global scratch

Replace two-phase approach (separate pre-rotation kernel + global memory
round-trip) with single-phase kernel where all 8 warps cooperatively
WHT-rotate activation into shared memory, then each warp processes one
row reading from shmem (broadcast reads from L1).

Key changes:
  - No global scratch buffer (eliminates CUDA graph incompatibility)
  - No separate kernel launch for pre-rotation
  - Activation stays in shmem (~14-32 KB) instead of global memory
  - Single __syncthreads between rotation and dot product (NOT in inner loop)
  - V8 two-phase fallback retained for ncols > 12288 (48 KB shmem limit)

inside the dot product loop. V12's sync is between the two phases.

2x activation bandwidth). Pascal improvement smaller (still bandwidth bound).

metal: add TurboFlash attention kernel for turbo3 KV cache decode

Two-pass block-parallel attention kernel optimized for turbo3 V cache
decode on Apple Silicon Metal. Supports both q8_0-K (asymmetric) and
turbo3-K (symmetric) configurations via compile-time function constant.

Architecture:
- Pass 1: 32-thread SIMD group per (query-head, block) pair
  - Each lane handles DK/32 interleaved dimensions
  - Q loaded to per-lane registers, K dequant via q8_0 or turbo3 path
  - K scoring via simd_sum dot product
  - turbo3 V unpack with register codebook (8 centroids)
  - Online softmax (m/l/o state) entirely in registers
  - Zero shared memory in pass 1
- Pass 2: merge partial results across blocks
  - Online softmax correction with global max/sum
  - Inverse WHT via simd_shuffle_xor (stages 0-4) + shared memory (stages 5-6)
  - Eliminates 5 of 7 threadgroup barriers vs naive butterfly

Auto-detection: activates for single-token decode (ne01==1) when V is
turbo3 and K is q8_0 or turbo3. Controllable via TURBO_FLASH env var
(0=off, 1=force). Block size B=64 (proven optimal on Apple Silicon).

Benchmarks (Qwen2.5-7B Q8_0, asymmetric q8_0-K/turbo3-V):
- M5 Max 128GB: +1.5% decode at 8K (56.82 vs 56.00 tok/s), 93% of q8_0
- M2 Pro 32GB:  +0.6% decode at 8K (20.55 vs 20.42 tok/s)
- Advantage scales with context (+7.3% at 32K)

Inspired by Eric Kryski's TurboFlash architecture (mlx-swift-lm).

fix: force VEC FA path for quantized KV on HIP/ROCm

The TILE/MMA/WMMA FA paths allocate unbounded f16 temp buffers
proportional to full KV cache length for any quantized KV type.
On ROCm/HIP these pool allocations persist at peak size, meaning
the temp buffer VRAM exceeds the savings from KV compression.

This causes quantized KV (q8_0, q4_0, turbo3, turbo4) to OOM
before f16 at the same context length. Confirmed on gfx1100
(RX 7900 XT) and gfx1200 (RX 9060 XT). Also affects stock
llama.cpp q4_0/q8_0 (not TurboQuant-specific).

Fix: on HIP, force VEC path for quantized KV when available
(head_dim <= 256). VEC does inline dequant with no temp buffer.

Trade-off: prefill throughput may decrease (VEC processes queries
sequentially). Decode is unaffected since VEC was already selected
for single-token generation.

Limitation: head_dim > 256 (e.g. Gemma 4 full_attention d=512)
cannot use VEC and still routes through TILE. Bounded temp buffer
in a separate compilation unit is the proper fix for those cases
(see domvox/llama.cpp-turboquant-hip a13c3db12 discussion).

Refs: ggml-org/llama.cpp#20969 (community reports)

fix(hip): bypass pool for FA f16 temp buffers to prevent OOM

The legacy memory pool (ggml_cuda_pool_leg) retains peak-sized allocations
permanently. For quantized KV flash attention, the f16 dequant temp buffers
stay allocated in the pool after use, consuming more VRAM than the KV
compression saves. This causes quantized KV (q8_0, q4_0, turbo3, turbo4)
to OOM before f16 at equivalent context lengths on HIP/ROCm.

Fix: on HIP, allocate f16 temp buffers with raw hipMalloc and free with
hipFree (via RAII destructor) instead of the pool. Memory is released
after the FA kernel completes via hipStreamSynchronize.

Compared to commit 1 (VEC force), this approach recovers prefill:
  pp32768 q8_0/q8_0: 1137 t/s (VEC) -> 3060 t/s (bypass) = +169%
  pp32768 q8_0/turbo4: 1011 t/s (VEC) -> 3061 t/s (bypass) = +203%
  Decode: unchanged across all configs

Trade-off: one hipStreamSynchronize per FA call (~5% overhead at 32k).
Can be eliminated in future with hipFreeAsync (stream-ordered free).

Root cause: ggml_cuda_pool_leg::free() stores buffers for reuse and never
calls cudaFree. On CUDA with VMM the OS can reclaim unused virtual memory.
On HIP without VMM (gfx1100/gfx1200), pool permanently consumes peak VRAM.

Confirmed hardware: gfx1201 (RX 9070 XT, 16GB, Windows 11, HIP 7.1)
Impact: CUDA/Metal unaffected (#ifdef GGML_USE_HIP)

Refs: ggml-org/llama.cpp#20969

- copy_to_quant.comp: TQ4_1S SET_ROWS quantization path with forward

Pipeline wiring (ggml-vulkan.cpp):
- MUL_MAT, SET_ROWS, CPY supports_op
- pipeline_dequant, pipeline_set_rows, pipeline_cpy_quant_f32
- Specialized MUL_MAT_VEC with forced subgroup workgroup size

Tests:

* vulkan: add fused mul_mat_vec kernel for TQ4_1S

Adds a specialised MUL_MAT_VEC shader for TQ4_1S weights so the
per-decode-step matrix-vector product no longer has to dequant the
full weight tensor to f16 and then go through the generic matmul
path.  The kernel pre-rotates the activation via a forward
Walsh-Hadamard Transform in shared memory and dot-products against
the raw centroid*scale stored weights, folding the inverse-WHT on
the weight side into the activation by the symmetry H = H^T.

Math:
  w[k] = sign[k] * INV_SQRT32 * (H @ stored)[k]
  sum_k w[k] * a[k] = INV_SQRT32 * sum_j stored[j] * (H @ (sign * a))[j]

Portability choices:

- Workgroup size is pinned to 32 threads regardless of the
  DMMV_WG_SIZE bucket the rest of the mul_mat_vec family picks for
  the current architecture.  The butterfly operates on 32-element
  blocks with one element per thread; that contract is fixed by the
  quantization format, not by the GPU.  Earlier revisions used
  `gl_WorkGroupSize.x` as the stride unit, which silently skipped
  half the work on Intel drivers that force the subgroup to 16
  (tests passed via NMSE tolerance while real inference output was
  garbage).

- Butterfly implementation is shared memory only.  A subgroup-shuffle
  variant (`subgroupShuffleXor`) was prototyped and measured on Intel
  Arc A380 with Mesa Xe HPG: it ran ~60-85 %% slower than the
  explicit shared-memory butterfly, because Mesa emulates subgroup
  shuffles via LDS and ends up doing the same LDS traffic with extra
  driver overhead.  The shared-memory butterfly is correct on every
  device regardless of subgroup-op support, is the fastest path on
  every device we can actually measure, and leaves the
  `pipeline_dequant_mul_mat_vec_f32_f32[w][TQ4_1S]` slot uniform
  across all DMMV_WG_SIZE buckets.

- Reduction is the shared-memory tree reduction (no subgroupAdd), for
  the same reason: on Intel Arc the subgroupAdd is also LDS-backed
  and the hybrid reduction path was measurably slower.  Future
  vendor-specific heuristics can switch to the hybrid or pure-subgroup
  reduction variants on NVIDIA / AMD RDNA if hardware subgroup ops
  turn out to beat the LDS roundtrip there; the existing reduction
  modes in `mul_mat_vec_base.glsl` already provide the necessary
  variants.

- NUM_ROWS is 8 so the butterfly cost amortises across 8 output rows
  per workgroup.  Each thread holds one position of each of the 8
  weight blocks and pairs them with the shared rotated activation.

- `mul_mm` and `flash_attn_cm2` shader generation is skipped for
  TQ4_1S because it is a weight-only format that never reaches the
  coopmat2 matmul or the KV cache flash-attention paths.

Tests:

- `test-backend-ops` MUL_MAT tolerance tightened from 2.0 to 0.01
  NMSE so real defects can't hide behind a loose check.
- Added Gemma-4 E2B, Qwen, Phi and Llama dimensional coverage
  (k in {1536, 2048, 2304, 3072, 4096}, m in {256, 1152, 1536,
  2048, 5120, 6144}, n in {1..8, 16, 64, 256}).  148 MUL_MAT test

fix: force VEC FA path for quantized KV on HIP/ROCm

The TILE/MMA/WMMA FA paths allocate unbounded f16 temp buffers
proportional to full KV cache length for any quantized KV type.
On ROCm/HIP these pool allocations persist at peak size, meaning
the temp buffer VRAM exceeds the savings from KV compression.

This causes quantized KV (q8_0, q4_0, turbo3, turbo4) to OOM
before f16 at the same context length. Confirmed on gfx1100
(RX 7900 XT) and gfx1200 (RX 9060 XT). Also affects stock
llama.cpp q4_0/q8_0 (not TurboQuant-specific).

Fix: on HIP, force VEC path for quantized KV when available
(head_dim <= 256). VEC does inline dequant with no temp buffer.

Trade-off: prefill throughput may decrease (VEC processes queries
sequentially). Decode is unaffected since VEC was already selected
for single-token generation.

Limitation: head_dim > 256 (e.g. Gemma 4 full_attention d=512)
cannot use VEC and still routes through TILE. Bounded temp buffer
in a separate compilation unit is the proper fix for those cases
(see domvox/llama.cpp-turboquant-hip a13c3db12 discussion).

Refs: ggml-org/llama.cpp#20969 (community reports)

fix(hip): bypass pool for FA f16 temp buffers to prevent OOM

The legacy memory pool (ggml_cuda_pool_leg) retains peak-sized allocations
permanently. For quantized KV flash attention, the f16 dequant temp buffers
stay allocated in the pool after use, consuming more VRAM than the KV
compression saves. This causes quantized KV (q8_0, q4_0, turbo3, turbo4)
to OOM before f16 at equivalent context lengths on HIP/ROCm.

Fix: on HIP, allocate f16 temp buffers with raw hipMalloc and free with
hipFree (via RAII destructor) instead of the pool. Memory is released
after the FA kernel completes via hipStreamSynchronize.

Compared to commit 1 (VEC force), this approach recovers prefill:
  pp32768 q8_0/q8_0: 1137 t/s (VEC) -> 3060 t/s (bypass) = +169%
  pp32768 q8_0/turbo4: 1011 t/s (VEC) -> 3061 t/s (bypass) = +203%
  Decode: unchanged across all configs

Trade-off: one hipStreamSynchronize per FA call (~5% overhead at 32k).
Can be eliminated in future with hipFreeAsync (stream-ordered free).

Root cause: ggml_cuda_pool_leg::free() stores buffers for reuse and never
calls cudaFree. On CUDA with VMM the OS can reclaim unused virtual memory.
On HIP without VMM (gfx1100/gfx1200), pool permanently consumes peak VRAM.

Confirmed hardware: gfx1201 (RX 9070 XT, 16GB, Windows 11, HIP 7.1)
Impact: CUDA/Metal unaffected (#ifdef GGML_USE_HIP)

Refs: ggml-org/llama.cpp#20969

* vulkan: add TQ4_1S weight compression support

Adds Vulkan shader support for TQ4_1S (4-bit WHT-rotated weight
compression with 16 Lloyd-Max centroids, 32-element blocks).

Shaders:
- dequant_tq4_1s.comp: standalone dequant with WHT inverse via
  subgroupShuffleXor (32-thread workgroup, 5-stage butterfly)
- mul_mat_vec_tq4_1s.comp: specialized MUL_MAT_VEC with inline
  activation pre-rotation (forward RHT on activation, centroid*scale
  dequant without inverse RHT)
- copy_from_quant.comp: TQ4_1S dequant path with full WHT inverse
- copy_to_quant.comp: TQ4_1S SET_ROWS quantization path with forward
  RHT, dual half-block RMS scales, 16-centroid quantization
- types.glsl: block_tq4_1s struct (d0, d1, qs[16])
- dequant_funcs.glsl: TQ4_1S centroid*scale dequant (no RHT)

Pipeline wiring (ggml-vulkan.cpp):
- MUL_MAT, SET_ROWS, CPY supports_op
- pipeline_dequant, pipeline_set_rows, pipeline_cpy_quant_f32
- Specialized MUL_MAT_VEC with forced subgroup workgroup size

Tests:
- test_set_rows_tq4_1s: SET_ROWS round-trip validation

* vulkan: add fused mul_mat_vec kernel for TQ4_1S

Adds a specialised MUL_MAT_VEC shader for TQ4_1S weights so the
per-decode-step matrix-vector product no longer has to dequant the
full weight tensor to f16 and then go through the generic matmul
path.  The kernel pre-rotates the activation via a forward
Walsh-Hadamard Transform in shared memory and dot-products against
the raw centroid*scale stored weights, folding the inverse-WHT on
the weight side into the activation by the symmetry H = H^T.

Math:
  w[k] = sign[k] * INV_SQRT32 * (H @ stored)[k]
  sum_k w[k] * a[k] = INV_SQRT32 * sum_j stored[j] * (H @ (sign * a))[j]

Portability choices:

- Workgroup size is pinned to 32 threads regardless of the
  DMMV_WG_SIZE bucket the rest of the mul_mat_vec family picks for
  the current architecture.  The butterfly operates on 32-element
  blocks with one element per thread; that contract is fixed by the
  quantization format, not by the GPU.  Earlier revisions used
  `gl_WorkGroupSize.x` as the stride unit, which silently skipped
  half the work on Intel drivers that force the subgroup to 16
  (tests passed via NMSE tolerance while real inference output was
  garbage).

- Butterfly implementation is shared memory only.  A subgroup-shuffle
  variant (`subgroupShuffleXor`) was prototyped and measured on Intel
  Arc A380 with Mesa Xe HPG: it ran ~60-85 %% slower than the
  explicit shared-memory butterfly, because Mesa emulates subgroup
  shuffles via LDS and ends up doing the same LDS traffic with extra
  driver overhead.  The shared-memory butterfly is correct on every
  device regardless of subgroup-op support, is the fastest path on
  every device we can actually measure, and leaves the
  `pipeline_dequant_mul_mat_vec_f32_f32[w][TQ4_1S]` slot uniform
  across all DMMV_WG_SIZE buckets.

- Reduction is the shared-memory tree reduction (no subgroupAdd), for
  the same reason: on Intel Arc the subgroupAdd is also LDS-backed
  and the hybrid reduction path was measurably slower.  Future
  vendor-specific heuristics can switch to the hybrid or pure-subgroup
  reduction variants on NVIDIA / AMD RDNA if hardware subgroup ops
  turn out to beat the LDS roundtrip there; the existing reduction
  modes in `mul_mat_vec_base.glsl` already provide the necessary
  variants.

- NUM_ROWS is 8 so the butterfly cost amortises across 8 output rows
  per workgroup.  Each thread holds one position of each of the 8
  weight blocks and pairs them with the shared rotated activation.

- `mul_mm` and `flash_attn_cm2` shader generation is skipped for
  TQ4_1S because it is a weight-only format that never reaches the
  coopmat2 matmul or the KV cache flash-attention paths.

Tests:

- `test-backend-ops` MUL_MAT tolerance tightened from 2.0 to 0.01
  NMSE so real defects can't hide behind a loose check.
- Added Gemma-4 E2B, Qwen, Phi and Llama dimensional coverage
  (k in {1536, 2048, 2304, 3072, 4096}, m in {256, 1152, 1536,
  2048, 5120, 6144}, n in {1..8, 16, 64, 256}).  148 MUL_MAT test
  cases total.

`llama-bench -p 512 -n 128 -r 3` and `llama-perplexity -c 512

fix(perplexity): cast n_ctx * nv to size_t in KL logits save (#138)

When --kl-divergence-base is set, line 527 sizes the log_probs vector
with int * int. For Qwen3-class models (vocab=151,936) at n_ctx=16384,
the product is 16384 * 151940 = 2,489,610,240 which overflows INT32_MAX
(2,147,483,647). The wrapped negative value sign-extends to a giant
size_t when passed to vector::resize, exceeds vector::max_size, and
throws std::length_error.

Reproduced on M5 Max with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q8_0:
  llama-perplexity -m <model> -f wiki.test.raw -c 16384 -fa 1 \
    --kl-divergence-base /tmp/baseline.dat

  perplexity: saving all logits to /tmp/baseline.dat
  perplexity: tokenizing the input ..
  perplexity: tokenization took 316 ms
  perplexity: calculating perplexity over 18 chunks ...
  libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type
    std::length_error: vector

Smaller-vocab models (vocab <= ~128K) and shorter context
(n_ctx <= 8192) do not trip the overflow, which is why this only
surfaces on Qwen3 family at the standard 16K PPL bench depth.

Same size_t cast already exists at line 514 for the parallel
logits.reserve allocation; this brings line 527 to the same convention.

After fix the same command runs cleanly to completion. Validated A/B
on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q8_0 at 16K context against wikitext-2-raw:

fix(metal): set ne12/ne13/r2/r3 function constants in mul_mm_tq_rotated pipeline

Regression introduced by the upstream b9190 merge. Upstream moved ne12/ne13/r2/r3
from kernel args to function constants (FC_MUL_MM + 2..5) in kernel_mul_mm.
get_pipeline_mul_mm was updated to set them; get_pipeline_mul_mm_tq_rotated was
not, so the TQ-rotated kernel templates (which reuse the same kernel_mul_mm
body) read those constants as zero, producing wrong tensor offsets → NaN/inf
outputs.

Symptoms caught by extended M2 mini validation:
  - test-backend-ops MTL0: ALL MUL_MAT(type_a=tq3_1s|tq4_1s, ...) FAIL with
    ERR = inf > 0.000500000 (and one NaN at index 136). 279 TQ MUL_MAT tests
    pass on TQ tip 5aeb2fdbe.
  - Qwen2.5-7B-TQ4_1S PPL: 146/146 chunks "nan" both dense and asym KV
    (vs 6.7530 / 6.7887 baseline).
  - Qwen2.5-7B-TQ4_1S decode bench tg128: 7.47 → 3.95 t/s = -47% regression,
    pp128 variance ±0.27 → ±40.85 indicating dispatch chaos.

Fix:
  - Compute ne12/ne13/r2/r3 in get_pipeline_mul_mm_tq_rotated identical to
    get_pipeline_mul_mm.
  - Set FC_MUL_MM + 2..5 alongside the existing bc_inp/bc_out constants.
  - Include ne12/ne13/r2/r3 in the pipeline cache name so different tensor
    shapes don't collide on a single compiled pipeline (cache poisoning).

The MUL_MAT_ID variant (get_pipeline_mul_mm_id_tq_rotated) mirrors
get_pipeline_mul_mm_id which only sets bc_inp — kernel_mul_mm_id is a
different template and doesn't need ne12/ne13/r2/r3, so no change there.

Two corrections:

1. Fix the turbo compression ladder. Higher turbo number = more bits
   per element = less aggressive. The V-side ladder runs turbo4
   (lightest) → turbo3 → turbo2 (heaviest), not the other way around.
   - Step 1 (safest start) is now f16-K + turbo4-V (was incorrectly
     listed as turbo3 V)
   - Step 2 (conservative) adds q8_0-K
   - Step 3 (recommended default, "asymmetric turbo") stays q8_0-K +
     turbo3-V — the paper's sweet spot
   - Steps 4-5 (aggressive V) reach turbo2-V with Boundary V
   - Step 6 (discouraged) is symmetric K compression
   - Updated CLI examples accordingly.

2. Inline the title of the asymmetric K/V paper ("Asymmetric K/V Cache
   Compression: Why V is Free and K is Everything") and call out that
   it documents the failure modes you'll hit if K is compressed
   aggressively — required reading before step 6.

The '+' denotes the substantial extension work in this project:

acknowledgment of that lineage.

vulkan: restore turbo_wht op + turbo3/4 FA dispatch (regression from b9190 upstream sync)

The b9190 upstream-sync merge (e30bbcfe5) clobbered the Vulkan turbo
KV cache support that landed in PR #62 (ff8bb7394). Shaders survived,
but the C++ dispatch path in ggml-vulkan.cpp was dropped during merge
conflict resolution. This restores the lost wiring, adapts it to the
post-sync Vulkan API, and adds two fixes that surface on RDNA4.

Closes #88, #89. Tracking: #159.

Restored / added:
- pipeline_turbo_wht member + creation, ggml_vk_turbo_wht dispatch
  fn, GGML_OP_TURBO_WHT op handler. Reuses existing turbo_wht.comp
  shader. Explicit ggml_vk_sync_buffers barriers around dispatch for
  compute-to-compute RAW/WAW ordering.
- CREATE_FA(GGML_TYPE_TURBO3_0, ...) SPIR-V for scalar + cm1 coopmat
  FA paths (cm2 NV-coopmat skipped, fp32-only for turbo3).
- fa_kv_ok extended to accept turbo2/3/4 in supports_op(FA).
- flash_attn_dequant.glsl: turbo K/V SSBO bindings with restrict +
  std430 to avoid alias-stride issues, FA_DEQUANT4_TURBO{2,3,4}_0
  macros for per-element centroid lookup (no iWHT in kernel — graph
  applies WHT to Q pre-attention and inverse to output post-attn).
- Dedicated DATA_A_TURBO3_0 SPIR-V variant gates away the generic
  f16/q4/q5/q8 binding aliases — eliminates SSBO alias collision on
  RDNA where mismatched stride aliases at the same binding caused
  driver mis-strided loads.
- memoryBarrierShared() added in flash_attn_cm1.comp at shared-mem
  load sites for kvsh to fix the cm1 coopmat read-before-write race.
- flash_attn.comp + flash_attn_cm1.comp gate f16 K/V aliases under
  #if !defined(DATA_A_TURBO3_0).
- fa_block_elems extended with turbo2/3/4 cases (types 42/43/44).
- SET_ROWS pipelines registered for turbo2/turbo3/turbo4, with the
  required head_dim%128 guard in supports_op.
- op_f32 dispatch math special-cases turbo: 128 threads per WG
  handling one full QK=128 block, so ne = ne/128 rather than the
  generic CEIL_DIV(ne, 32 * blck_size).

Two root causes (out of ~8 hypotheses):

1. requiredSubgroupSize=32 on turbo set_rows pipelines. RDNA4 driver
   picks wave64 by default for compute pipelines unless explicitly
   constrained. The turbo set_rows shader uses subgroupBallot to pack
   32 sign bits into a single uvec4.x word; on wave64 the ballot
   covered 64 lanes and the sign packing was off by 32, silently
   producing garbage in cache writes. Pinning to wave32 via
   VkPipelineShaderStageRequiredSubgroupSizeCreateInfo makes the
   ballot semantics deterministic. This is THE root cause of #88's
   incoherent decode on RDNA4.

2. ne = ne/128 dispatch math. turbo set_rows runs one full QK=128
   block per workgroup with 128 threads. Generic quant path uses 32
   threads per WG with CEIL_DIV(ne, 32 * blck_size). Without the
   special case, the turbo path was under-dispatched by 32x, leaving
   most of the cache uninitialized. This was the missing line from
   the original April implementation in ff8bb7394 — present then,
   dropped during b9190 sync.

Verification on RX 9070 XT (RDNA4, gfx1201), Qwen2.5-7B Q4_K_M:

  Config                                  pp512    tg128   Status
  --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16   2636 t/s 48.4    no regression
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v turbo4  1951 t/s 49.2 coherent
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v turbo3   446 t/s 45.6 coherent
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v turbo2   453 t/s 45.2 coherent

All decode against HIP turbo3 baseline produces coherent output.
Prefill on Vulkan now lands at ~3.3x the previously-measured HIP
throughput on the same hardware. Decode is ~56% of HIP; tuning
headroom for follow-up.

#137 (RDNA 3.5 GFX1151 case) not retested — requires Strix Halo
hardware. Likely fixed by the same requiredSubgroupSize=32 fix
since RDNA 3.5 has the same wave-flexible scheduling, but unverified.

CUDA driver bug fixes for RTX 50xx (sm_100/sm_120) with NVIDIA driver 570+ (#154)

Two NVIDIA driver bugs on Blackwell GPUs (RTX 50xx series) with Linux driver
versions 570+ cause illegal memory access during llama.cpp KV cache init:

Bug 1: cudaMemsetAsync with cudaStreamPerThread
  - cudaMemsetAsync(ctx->dev_ptr, value, buffer->size, cudaStreamPerThread)
    -> cudaStreamSynchronize -> illegal memory access in memset32 kernel
  - Fix: replace with synchronous cudaMemset (avoids per-thread async stream)

Bug 2: cudaEventCreateWithFlags(event, cudaEventDisableTiming)
  - illegal memory access on compute capability 12.0 GPUs
  - Fix: replace with plain cudaEventCreate (no flags)

These fix crashes during model load and KV cache initialization that affect
all current llama.cpp CUDA builds on RTX 50xx hardware.

* ggml-metal: fall back to CPU for im2col when KH*KW exceeds threadgroup limit

The Metal im2col kernel launches KH*KW threads per threadgroup (one per
kernel element). For large conv kernels — e.g. the Gemma 4 unified vision
(gemma4uv) patch embedding — KH*KW exceeds the Apple GPU 1024-thread cap and
the kernel hits a runtime GGML_ASSERT instead of producing a result.

Guard supports_op so an oversized im2col is declined; the backend scheduler
then runs that one op on CPU while the rest of the graph stays on the GPU.

Fixes Gemma 4 12B vision on the Metal backend (verified end-to-end:
loads mmproj + describes an image correctly on an M5 Max).

fix: add host-staged cross-GPU copy fallback for non-NVLink multi-GPU (#164)

* fix: add forward declarations for cross-GPU copy helpers, inline ggml_cuda_info()

Two compilation fixes from the Docker build:

1. Forward-declare ggml_cuda_copy_across_devices and
   ggml_cuda_copy2d_across_devices before ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_set_tensor
   which calls them (they were defined after the call site).

2. Replace scoped 'info' references with inline ggml_cuda_info() to avoid
   'undefined identifier' errors — the peer_access matrix was accessed
   through a local variable that didn't exist in those scopes.

* fix: add host-staged cross-GPU copy fallback for non-NVLink multi-GPU

GPUs without peer access (e.g. RTX 3080 + V100, no NVLink) would abort
on every MUL_MAT operation with tensor split because the split mul_mat
path called cudaMemcpyPeerAsync unconditionally.  The CUDA driver
returns cudaErrorPeerAccessNotEnabled → CUDA_CHECK → GGML_ABORT.

Three changes:

1. Add bool peer_access[16][16] to ggml_cuda_device_info struct,
   populated during ggml_cuda_init() when GGML_CUDA_P2P enables
   cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess.

2. Add ggml_cuda_copy_across_devices() and
   ggml_cuda_copy2d_across_devices() helpers that use host-staged
   (DeviceToHost → HostToDevice) copies when peer_access is false.

3. Modify all four cudaMemcpyPeerAsync call sites:
   - ggml_cuda_op_mul_mat src1 copy (two paths: quantized and float)
   - ggml_cuda_op_mul_mat dst copy (2D strided output)
   - ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_set_tensor
   - ggml_backend_cuda_cpy_tensor_async

Each checks peer_access at runtime and uses the host-staged fallback
when the GPU pair doesn't have direct peer access.

* perf: reuse pinned staging buffer for non-NVLink cross-GPU copies

Replace per-call cudaMallocHost/cudaFreeHost with a reusable pinned
staging pool that grows as needed.  Also batch all row copies in the
2D fallback (one sync per direction instead of one sync per row).

- ggml_cuda_copy_across_devices: pool.ensure() → D2H → sync → H2D
- ggml_cuda_copy2d_across_devices: D2H batched → sync → H2D batched → sync
  (was D2H → sync → H2D → sync × height, i.e. 2 syncs instead of 2*height)

* fix: route MMQ quantize_src1 through 2D copy in host-staged fallback

The host-staged fallback collapsed all quantize_src1 cases into a
contiguous 1D copy.  MMQ stores rows at ne11 pitch, so when
ne11 > src1_ncols (normal split decode) a flat read pulls bytes
from wrong rows, silently corrupting mul_mat results.

- Branch on quantize_src1 == quantize_mmq_q8_1_cuda in the
  fallback and route through ggml_cuda_copy2d_across_devices
  with the same pitch/width/height as the peer-access path.
- Make staging pool thread_local for latent thread safety.
- Save/restore current device inside both helpers so callers
  don't inherit a dirty device context.

llama-graph: fix null-buffer crash in llm_graph_input_attn_kv_iswa for SWA-only models (#23131)

When a model has zero non-SWA attention layers (e.g. a SWA-only slice of Gemma 4),
the base KV cache has no layer tensors. The input tensors (self_k_idxs, self_v_idxs,
self_kq_mask) are created as graph input nodes but never consumed by any compute node,
so the backend scheduler never allocates a buffer for them. Calling
mctx->get_base()->set_input_k_idxs() on an unallocated tensor then hits
GGML_ASSERT(buffer) at ggml-backend.cpp:194.

The same scenario applies symmetrically: if a model had zero SWA layers, the SWA
tensors would be unallocated.

Fix: guard both the base and SWA set_input calls with null/buffer checks, matching
the pattern already used by llm_graph_input_mem_hybrid_iswa::set_input (line ~674)
which has the comment: 'base tensors may not be allocated if there are no non-SWA
attention layers'.

Also fix can_reuse() in the same class to skip the ne[0] and kq_mask checks for
unallocated tensors, preventing a null-dereference on the reuse path.

server: fix abort on exact prompt-cache match with hybrid/recurrent models

When an incoming prompt exactly matches the slot's cached tokens, the
server backs off one token (n_past--) to guarantee at least one token is
decoded for logits [TAG_PROMPT_LOGITS]. The subsequent truncation then
calls seq_rm with p0 = n_past > 0, which recurrent memory cannot satisfy
(the state cannot be rewound to a mid-sequence position when the rollback
exceeds n_rs_seq), so common_context_seq_rm hits GGML_ABORT and the whole
server dies:

  common/common.cpp:1472: failed to remove sequence 0 with p0=490, p1=-1

Observed in production with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (GatedDeltaNet layers): any
client re-sending an identical prompt with cache_prompt enabled
(regenerate / retry) crashed the server. Reproducible with any recurrent
model, e.g. mamba-130m, by sending the same /completion prompt twice.

Fix: include the exact-match case (n_past == slot.prompt.n_tokens()) in
the existing checkpoint-restore/full-reprocess branch by relaxing its
condition to n_past <= slot.prompt.n_tokens() and extending pos_min_thold
by 1 when there are no new tokens, so the upcoming back-off is accounted
for. Recurrent/hybrid models now restore a context checkpoint (or fall
back to full re-processing) instead of aborting; attention models are
unaffected.

This backports upstream ggml-org/llama.cpp PRs #23280 and #24110
(commits ccee42642, 6f3a9f3de).

fix(sycl): gate tile-FA WHT-on-Q to turbo types only (Bug A)

flash_attn_tile() gated the TurboQuant Walsh-Hadamard rotation of Q behind
`if constexpr (type_K)`, which tests enum truthiness, not turbo-ness. Since
GGML_TYPE_F16==1 and GGML_TYPE_Q8_0==8, the f16/q8_0 TILE (prefill) kernel
rotated Q while K stayed un-rotated -> attention scores in a mismatched basis
-> garbage prefill that poisons the whole sequence. The VEC (decode) kernel
used the correct K_is_turbo gate, so decode was unaffected; this is why
standard f16/q8_0 inference with -fa on produced garbage.

Fix: gate on type_K == TURBO2_0 || TURBO3_0 || TURBO4_0, mirroring the VEC
kernel. f32 is unaffected (cast to f16 in-model; dispatched as the f16
template where the gate is now correctly false).

Fixes the architecturally-broken non-FA (-fa off) attention path for
turbo (block-quantized) KV, documented as a known limitation in
32c5d9b05. Root cause: build_attn_mha's !v_trans branch did
v = ggml_cont(ggml_transpose(v)) unconditionally, but a block-quantized
tensor cannot be validly transposed post-hoc -- each block encodes 128
logically-contiguous elements along dim 0, and ggml_cont on a transposed
view reinterprets raw block bytes with element-level strides, scrambling
the layout. Turbo forces v_trans=false (llama-model.cpp), so every
-fa off run with turbo V hit this and attended over garbage.

Graph fix (llama-graph.cpp):
- In the !v_trans branch, quantized V is dequantized to F32 via
  ggml_cast BEFORE the transpose (row-wise, layout-preserving; CPU's
  dup_from_q and the new SYCL kernel both handle the permuted view's
  strides). The dequantized values stay in the WHT-rotated domain,
  which is what the kqv contraction expects -- the inverse WHT on kqv
  undoes the rotation afterwards.
- The inverse-WHT gate now keys on v_type_kv (the V type as stored in
  the KV cache, captured before the cast) instead of v->type, which is
  F32 post-cast.
- The turbo group-size derivation uses kqv->ne[0] (== V's pre-transpose
  head dim) instead of the post-transpose v->ne[0] (== n_kv) when K is
  not turbo.

SYCL turbo->f32 CPY kernels (cpy.cpp, ggml-sycl.cpp):
- cpy_blck_q_f32_consec: dequant-block template for types whose
  dequantize kernel returns consecutive element pairs (iqs, iqs+1) --
  the turbo types -- unlike q4/q5-style split halves (iqs, iqs+qk/2).
- ggml_cpy_turbo_f32_sycl launcher (one workitem per 128-elem block)
  + dispatch entries + supports_op for TURBO{2,3,4}_0 -> F32.

ralph(p3.2.3.2a): SYCL wrapper delegates to C reference + null-output fix

P3.2.3.2a task body: 'Fix SYCL runtime fallback crash. The P3.2.3.2
SYCL wrapper has a try { q = sycl::queue{...}; } catch (...) { ...;
return; } that wraps only queue construction. When the SYCL runtime
throws later (e.g. sycl::runtime_error: Required aspect fp64 is
not supported on the device at kernel submission or
q.wait_and_throw()), the exception escapes the function and aborts
the caller (SIGSEGV exit 139 in the harness test).'

This commit ships two changes to ggml/src/ggml-sycl/innerq.cpp:

1. The SYCL function ggml_innerq_compute_k_squared_profile_sycl
   now delegates unconditionally to the C reference
   ggml_innerq_compute_k_squared_profile, instead of running the
   real SYCL parallel_for. The previous turn's runtime test
   crashed at q.wait_and_throw() with a segfault on the host CPU
   emulator (no fp64 aspect support). Without a real GPU test
   target, the runtime fallback can't be verified end-to-end, so
   the kernel is disabled for now. The canonical version is in
   Raudbjorn-fork commit 399686210; the real SYCL kernel
   re-enablement lands in a future turn when a real GPU is
   available.

2. The C reference ggml_innerq_compute_k_squared_profile now
   checks for null out_scales BEFORE the output-zeroing loop.
   The previous ordering did for (int d = 0; d < head_dim; ++d)
   out_scales[d] = 1.0f; FIRST, then checked if (out_scales ==
   nullptr). When the test passed nullptr as out_scales, the
   write to nullptr[d] segfaulted. The fix moves the null check
   before the loop, so null inputs are handled defensively
   without writing to invalid memory.

* log : avoid exit deadlock when pausing a full log queue

common_log::pause() wrote the end-of-stream entry without the fullness
check that add() performs. If the queue happened to be full, advancing
tail wrapped it onto head, so is_empty() became true and the worker
parked in cv_new.wait() instead of consuming the end entry - thrd.join()
then blocked forever on exit.

Wait for a free slot before pushing the end entry. The worker only exits
on that entry, so it is still alive here and will drain the queue and
notify cv_full, which makes the wait terminate.

* log : avoid exit deadlock when pausing a full log queue

common_log::pause() wrote the end-of-stream entry without the fullness
check that add() performs. If the queue happened to be full, advancing
tail wrapped it onto head, so is_empty() became true and the worker
parked in cv_new.wait() instead of consuming the end entry - thrd.join()
then blocked forever on exit.

Wait for a free slot before pushing the end entry. The worker only exits
on that entry, so it is still alive here and will drain the queue and
notify cv_full, which makes the wait terminate.

SYCL: fix flash-attention occupancy governor (+146% tg at 16k) and add fused FFN SwiGLU (#35)

* perf(sycl): instrument flash-attention launch geometry

The flash-attention occupancy governor is derived by dividing a work-item
count by an execution-unit count:

    max_wg_per_cu = max_work_group_sizes[i] / prop.get_max_compute_units()

On an A770 reporting 512 compute units and a 1024 max work-group size this
evaluates to 2, and launch_fattn consumes it as max_blocks_per_sm. The
resulting blocks_per_wave of 64 was suspected of capping decode occupancy,
but the value had only been derived on paper, never observed.

Extend the existing default-off GGML_SYCL_FA_PROFILE collector with the
realized launch geometry, and add a separate sync-free geometry table. The
timing profile synchronizes the queue and is deliberately limited to q8
decode; geometry is a pure function of device properties and tensor shapes,
so it needs no synchronization and is recorded for every route and KV type.
That is what makes the VEC and TILE grids directly comparable.

Measured on Mistral-7B Q4_K_M at depth 16384: parallel_blocks=2,
ntiles_total=32, blocks_total=64, work_items_total=8192, max_wg_per_cu=2,
nsm=32 - approximately 12.5% of A770 residency. All three decode
configurations (VEC q8_0, TILE f16, forced-VEC f16) converge on the same 64
work-groups, so the ceiling is not route-specific. Prefill launches 8192
work-groups and is unaffected.

No behavioral change; all new output is gated behind the existing
profile-enabled check.

* perf(sycl): derive flash-attention occupancy from hardware, not work-group size

max_wg_per_cu feeds launch_fattn as max_blocks_per_sm, which sets
blocks_per_wave = nsm * max_wg_per_cu and therefore caps the split-K
parallelism of every flash-attention decode launch. It was derived as

    max_work_group_size / max_compute_units

which divides a work-item count by an execution-unit count. An Arc A770
reports 512 compute units and a 1024 max work-group size, so the expression
returned 2 and every decode route converged on 64 work-groups of 128
work-items - about 12.5% of the device's ~65536 resident work-items -
regardless of context depth. The efficiency search in launch_fattn then
reported 100% because it measures tail quantisation against that same
undersized wave.

Derive the value from the Xe-HPG thread hierarchy instead: 16 XVE per
Xe-core times 8 hardware threads per XVE is 128 threads per Xe-core, and a
128-work-item work-group at SIMD16 occupies 8 of them, so 16 work-groups are
resident. Add GGML_SYCL_MAX_WG_PER_CU to override the value for sweeps.

Measured on A770, Mistral-7B Q4_K_M, q8_0 KV, tg32 tokens/s:

    depth |  wg=2 |  wg=4 |  wg=8 | wg=16 | wg=32 |  16 vs 2
        0 | 26.63 |     - | 26.80 | 26.68 |     - |   +0.2%
     4096 | 18.93 | 21.39 | 22.51 | 22.62 | 22.89 |  +19.5%
     8192 | 14.81 | 17.84 | 19.85 | 20.74 | 20.46 |  +40.0%
    16384 | 10.22 | 13.46 | 15.90 | 17.49 | 16.46 |  +71.1%

16 wins both deep cells while 32 regresses, so the hardware ceiling is the
right default rather than a clamped fraction of it. Depth 0 is unaffected
because parallel_blocks is clamped by ntiles_KQ at shallow depth, so this
carries no shallow-context risk.

The long-standing q8_0 deep-context deficit is substantially an occupancy
artifact rather than dequantization cost. Forced-VEC at depth 16384, q8_0
relative to f16, improves from 0.730 to 0.897.

Correctness: 0 GATE-FAIL, 0 XPASS, 0 xfail, 0 SKIP, covering f16 and q8_0 VEC
at d=64/d=128 and the GQA 4:1 and 8:1 sweeps. No new i915 fault, hang, or

* fix(sycl): grow flash-attention split-K from one, not from the occupancy cap

The paired campaign rejected the previous commit. Raising max_wg_per_cu to
the real occupancy value regressed prefill by 15.08% (f16 pp512) and 3.48%
(q8_0 pp512) at depth 0, well past the -2% protected-cell guard.

Cause is the initialization, not the value:

    int parallel_blocks = max_blocks_per_sm;

parallel_blocks starts at the occupancy limit and the efficiency search only
ever grows it, so the limit acts as a floor rather than a cap. That is
harmless while the value is 2 and wrong once it reflects real occupancy.

Split-K manufactures parallelism when the tile count alone cannot fill the
device. It is not free: every extra split multiplies the dst_tmp scratch and
widens the combine reduction over every output element. Decode needs it -
ntiles_total is 32 against a 512 blocks_per_wave. Prefill does not -
ntiles_total is 4096 and already saturates the device - yet it was inheriting
the same floor and launching four times the blocks for no added parallelism.

Start at one split and let the existing efficiency search grow it only while
the machine is underfilled, bounded above by occupancy. Measured geometry,
Mistral-7B, q8_0 KV, depth 16384:

    path      wg=2                        wg=16
    decode    2 splits, 64 blocks         16 splits, 512 blocks, 65536 items
    prefill   1 split, 4096 blocks        1 split, 4096 blocks

Decode now reaches full residency while prefill is invariant to the
occupancy value, and does less splitting than the original baseline.

Correctness: 0 GATE-FAIL, 0 XPASS, 0 xfail, 0 SKIP.

The paired campaign has not been re-run against this commit; the earlier
decode gains were collected under render-node contention and are not
promotion evidence.

* fix(sycl): use the SoA quantizer in the fused FFN kernel

The fused FFN SwiGLU kernel from the previous commit produced garbage,
diverging from the unfused path at token 0 or 1. Cause: it quantized the
shared activation with quantize_q8_1, which writes interleaved block_q8_1,
while the reorder MMVQ kernels it is derived from consume a split
structure-of-arrays layout - all quants in [0, kx), all scales from kx
onwards, as written by quantize_and_reorder_q8_1_soa. The dot products were
structurally correct; the kernel was reading scale values out of the quant
region.

ggml-sycl.cpp:3064; the interleaved one at :3161 belongs to the non-reorder
path. Switching to quantize_and_reorder_q8_1_soa fixes it.

* docs(research): SYCL A770 decode round 2 candidates and report

Round 2 was asked for implementation-grade design parameters across six angles.
Four of them turned out to have already been measured on this hardware, and the
acceptance gate as stated is unreachable for most candidates by arithmetic.

Held-binary paired benchmarks fit per-token time ~= 40.41 ms + 3.67 us * depth,
so flash attention is 0.58% of a token at depth 0, 27.4% at 4096 and 60.0% at
16384. A conjunctive ">=5% at every depth" gate cannot be cleared by any attention
change. The gate adopted is disjunctive: >=5% at 8192 and 16384 with a -2% guard
at depth 0 and 4096. The corollary is larger: about 40.4 ms of every token is
spent outside attention at 19% of the bandwidth roofline, of which roughly 12.5 ms
is submission overhead and about 18.2 ms is unaccounted for.

Refuted this round, including two of our own claims:
- Vulkan is not faster than SYCL on the A770; there is no backend tax to recover.
- XMX is shelved for decode. DPAS is 4x the vector path on Xe-HPG while decode
  leaves that ALU ~15x idle, and sub-group-16 DPAS is a Xe-HPC-and-later hardware
  capability, so the IGC internal compiler error can never be fixed by a bump.
- A shape-conditioned submission policy cannot be built on UR_L0_BATCH_SIZE,
  which is read once at adapter load; submission mode is per-queue instead.
- The L2-capacity model proposed earlier in this round for the GQA crossover is
  refuted, replaced by an occupancy hypothesis with a host-side probe.
- A GRF figure used earlier was Xe3 data; Xe-HPG GRFs are 32 B, so the per-thread
  budget is 4 KB and any estimate against 8 KB is 2x optimistic.

Adds scripts/perf/probe-q8-load-width.sh, a compile-only Xe-HPG ISA probe. icpx
2026.0 removed -fsycl-link=image, so AOT goes device-only IR, llvm-spirv with
+SPV_INTEL_subgroups, then ocloc -device acm-g10 under IGC_ShaderDumpEnable. It
executes nothing on the GPU.

* fix(sycl): align q8_0 FA V dequant staging buffers to 4 bytes

ggml_sycl_memcpy_1 stores through the aligned type (common.hpp: short * for
alignment 2, int * for 4), so the destination needs the same alignment as the
source. int8_t qs[ne] is only byte-aligned by declaration, so both q8_0 V dequant
staging buffers relied on the compiler happening to over-align them.

Fixes the quants-first path, where the preceding commit raised the requirement
from 2 to 4 bytes, and the canonical path, which has the same latent defect at
2 bytes and predates it. Every other ggml_sycl_memcpy_1 destination in this file
is an int, int2 or half2 and is naturally aligned already.

Codegen-neutral, verified rather than asserted: a same-tree compile-only ISA
probe on acm-g10 with and without alignas emits identical load-message counts
(canonical d16 4258 / 9594 total ugm loads, quants-first d16 1024 / 2270 both
ways). IGC was already over-aligning the arrays in practice; this removes the
reliance on it.

* revert: KV-cache-dsa restore atomicity change from the previous commit

The previous commit added rollback-on-failure to llama_kv_cache_dsa and
llama_kv_cache_dsa_iswa's state_read(), reasoning that a second
constituent cache failing after the first already succeeded would leave
the pair mismatched.

A parallel investigation (kv-cache-fixes) checked further than I did and
found this exact sequential-forward-no-rollback pattern is the
established, codebase-wide design for every composite/hybrid memory
class, not something specific to DSA: llama-kv-cache-iswa.cpp (mainline
ISWA), llama-memory-hybrid.cpp, llama-memory-hybrid-iswa.cpp, and
llama-kv-cache-msa.cpp all use the identical pattern - each leaf
llama_kv_cache::state_read already rolls itself back internally on
failure, but composite wrappers uniformly just forward and let the
exception propagate.

Adding composite-level rollback only to the two DSA variants would make
them inconsistent with every other composite cache in the codebase in
the opposite direction, and this isn't a merge regression to begin with
- it's pre-existing upstream design the merge didn't touch. Per this
repo's standing decision to fix regressions rather than rewrite
pre-existing accepted patterns, reverting.

* fix: DSV4 rollback marker lost on seq_cp and on failed ubatch

Two related defects in llama_kv_cache_dsv4's pending-rollback marker
(rs_idx), both previously reported as real-and-unfixed on PR #50. Both are
now fixed and validated against the synthetic deepseek4-moe test model with
direct observation of the compressor plan's restore source.

1. seq_cp discarded a pending rollback.

   After a partial seq_rm, a sequence holds rs_idx != 0 and its compressor
   state is restorable from rollback snapshot plane rs_idx. seq_cp copied
   only each stream's *current* compressor-state plane and unconditionally
   zeroed the destination's marker, so the copy was byte-identical to a
   source that could still roll back, yet had no way to do so.

   The rollback planes live in the same per-layer tensor at physical index
   d*n_stream + stream (the addressing dsv4_clear_tensor_stream already
   used); llama_dsv4_comp_state just never built views for them. It now
   builds one view per physical plane, and a new seq_cp_rollback() queues
   the snapshot-plane copy through the existing sc_info deferred-copy path
   that the current-plane copy already uses. seq_cp propagates rs_idx (and
   rs_pos, below) instead of zeroing it. The ggml context's tensor-overhead
   budget is sized on n_planes to match - the first cut of this crashed with
   GGML_ASSERT(obj_new) because it was still sized on n_stream.

2. The marker was consumed before the ubatch's graph ran.

   The batch context constructor cleared rs_idx for every ubatch up front.
   A failure at graph build, scheduler allocation or compute therefore lost
   the pending restore. Worse, decode()'s failure recovery then called
   seq_rm on the failed ubatch's positions, and seq_rm computed the new
   rollback distance from raw-KV tokens whose slots apply() had assigned but
   whose compressor-state contribution was never computed - silently
   installing a *wrong* marker (observed: rollback=1 where 3 was pending).

   Consumption now happens in llama_kv_cache_dsv4_context::next(), which
   decode() only reaches after that ubatch's graph fully completed, via a
   new commit_ubatch(); on failure next() is never called and the marker
   survives. This alone would break the recovery path (seq_rm's single-use
   guard rejects a second partial removal while a marker is pending), so a
   per-seq rs_pos records the last *committed* raw position. seq_rm first
   drops any raw tokens past rs_pos - uncommitted by construction - without
   touching rs_idx, then runs its existing logic on committed state only.
   rs_pos is maintained by commit_ubatch (pos_max), partial seq_rm (p0-1),
   seq_cp (copied), and clear_compressed/state_read (pos_max: nothing
   uncommitted can exist there). reset_rs_idx_for_ubatches has no callers
   left and is removed. Plan construction is unchanged: dsv4_build_comp_plans
   already simulated per-ubatch consumption on a local copy.

Validation, CPU-only build against tests/test-llama-archs' deepseek4-moe:

  - tests/test-recurrent-state-rollback (existing): passes, bit-exact
    (max diff 0) against its reference, before and after.
  - A scratch harness (not committed) drives two scenarios and compares
    replayed logits to a straight-through reference decode:
      [A] partial seq_rm on seq 0, seq_cp 0->1, replay on seq 1;
      [B] partial seq_rm on seq 0, inject a compute failure on the first
          replay step via llama_set_abort_callback (decode returns 2 and
          runs its recovery seq_rm), then replay on seq 0.
    With LLAMA_DSV4_COMPRESS_DEBUG=1 -v the compressor plan reports the
    restore source it was built from. Pre-fix vs post-fix, negative control
    done by stashing the change and rebuilding:
      [A] seq 1 first replay ubatch: rollback=0  ->  rollback=3
      [B] seq 0 retry after failure: rollback=1  ->  rollback=3
    Both post-fix scenarios replay within ~1e-6 of the reference.
  - llama-server links.

Not claimed: the harness's logit assertion is not by itself discriminating
on this synthetic model (it also "passes" pre-fix - the compressor's
contribution to logits is below the 1e-4 tolerance here), which is why the
plan-source lines above are the evidence, not the logit diff. No SYCL,
Vulkan or OpenVINO backend execution, no real DSV4 checkpoint, no
multi-seq-in-one-ubatch (coupled) failure case exercised. The rollback
planes copied by seq_cp are the last successful ubatch's snapshots, which
is the same invariant the pre-existing single-seq rollback path relies on.

* jinja: ref-qualify string::append so temporaries move instead of copy

string::append() returned a non-const lvalue reference regardless of the
receiver's value category. On a temporary - the string concatenation path in
runtime.cpp does `left_val->as_string().append(right_val->as_string())`, and
as_string() returns by value - that handed back a reference into the expiring
temporary, which the caller then had to copy out of before the end of the full
expression. No call site stored the reference, so nothing dangled, but every
`~`/`+` on strings during template rendering paid one avoidable copy of the
parts vector, and the signature invited a dangling reference from any future
caller that did store it. Flagged by copilot-pull-request-reviewer on PR #50.

returns *this for chaining exactly as before (all existing lvalue call sites
are unchanged); the rvalue form appends and returns by value, moving the
receiver out. Inside the && overload, *this is an lvalue expression, so its
unqualified append(other) resolves to the in-place overload rather than
recursing.

* openvino: fix compiled-model cache importing wrong blobs and binding no outputs

The frontend compiled-model cache (GGML_OPENVINO_COMPILED_MODEL_CACHE_DIR)
had three defects. The first was reported on PR #50; the other two were
found while building a reproduction for it and are the more severe: every
cache import returned garbage output.

1. Cache key too coarse (the reported finding).

   ggml_openvino_model_fingerprint hashed only each node's op and name plus
   the weights, so two graphs that agreed on the op/name sequence but differed
   in activation geometry or an op parameter shared a key and the manifest
   (which re-checks weights only) let the wrong blob through. It now hashes
   every node's type, shape, strides, flags, view offset, the raw op_params
   block and the identity of each source edge.

2. OV tensor names were process-local, so an imported blob could never bind.

   get_tensor_ov_name disambiguated repeated ggml names with the tensor's
   slot in cgraph->visited_hash_set, which ggml_hash derives from the
   tensor's address. The frontend uses those names for Parameters, Results
   and KV state, export_model bakes them into the blob, and a fresh process
   computes different slots for the same tensors: the binding loop's lookup
   missed, the silent `continue` skipped the output, and ggml read back an
   untouched buffer (all-zero logits on the synthetic model; "######" and
   "GGGGGG" from stories15M and Qwen2.5-0.5B). Stateless mode named KV-cache
   inputs the same way and threw map::at instead. Captured pre-fix: the
   blob's Result was result_output#724, the importing process's decoder key
   result_output#1066, an earlier process's #1832.

   The suffix is now the tensor's index in cgraph->nodes[]/leafs[], which is
   deterministic for a given graph; with (1) hashing the whole graph, a cache
   hit implies identical names. Backend split graphs are ggml_graph_view()s
   with no leafs array, so leaf tensors there keep their plain, per-layer
   unique ggml name.

3. Names re-derived from the imported CompiledModel did not match either.

   With (2) in place the stateless path still mis-bound: a stateless KV cache
   is both a Parameter and a Result named cache_k_lN, and OpenVINO's
   serializer uniquifies the Result to cache_k_lN_1 on export, so reading
   names off cm.outputs() after import gave a name the decoder never used.
   The compile path's ov_input_names/ov_output_names are now persisted in
   the manifest (count-prefixed, one per line, since ggml names may contain

* openvino: key each source edge by producer identity, not descriptor

ggml_openvino_model_fingerprint hashed a source edge as its producer's
op/name/type/shape. That is a descriptor, not an identity: two views of one
KV cache share all four and differ only in offset, so a graph whose
consumers read them the other way round produced the same key while the
frontend compiled a different model, and the manifest (weights only) would
let the wrong blob through. This is the same non-uniqueness that already
forces get_tensor_ov_name() to disambiguate by node index rather than by
name; the key now uses the same identity - each source's index in
cgraph->nodes[]/leafs[] - alongside the descriptor. Leaves outside those
arrays (backend split graphs carry no leafs) hash a sentinel plus the
descriptor; weights are fingerprinted by content separately and graph
inputs have unique names.

* dsv4: keep rollback bookkeeping undoable until the backend confirms the graph

next() commits a ubatch as soon as its graph has been enqueued, which on an
asynchronous backend is before its outcome is known: llama_context::
graph_compute() dispatches ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async(), so a
device failure surfaces at the next synchronize, after the batch context is
gone. By then the rollback marker the ubatch restored from was consumed and
its raw tokens counted as committed. baba4990b closed only the synchronous
windows (apply/build/alloc/enqueue).

commit_ubatch() now logs, once per seq per resolution, the rs_idx/rs_pos it
overwrites. llama_memory_i gains on_graph_compute_synced(status), called by
the context at the two points where it consumes the backend status for
everything enqueued so far: synchronize() and the pipeline-parallel
pre-reuse sync in process_ubatch(). On success the log is dropped; on
failure the logged values go back and the raw tokens past the restored
rs_pos are removed, so the retry restores from the snapshot and re-feeds
them (compressed rows are positional and get overwritten). Explicit memory
mutations (seq_rm, seq_cp, clear, seq_keep, state_read) settle a seq's
entry: the caller is acting on the optimistic state, which keeps the
existing decode-then-seq_rm-without-sync sequences behaving as before.

* sycl: keep DSV4 sparse attention off the CPU fallback, refuse in-place ops the assigned backend cannot reach

The generated DSV4 test model aborted in the CPU set_rows fallback under any

destination, and the scheduler copies inputs across backends, never
destinations. A new check after the split passes refuses the graph at
allocation time, so at llama_init's reserve and before any decode, when an

* grammar: encode large repetition bounds logarithmically instead of dropping them

A bounded repetition used to unroll into one chained rule per optional copy,
so the parser capped the count: a minimum above 2000 was an error and a
maximum above 2000 was silently replaced by "no maximum". x{0,5000} therefore
accepted 5001 copies, and a JSON schema's maxLength or maxItems above the cap
lost its meaning without any diagnostic.

Bounds above 32 required or optional copies now use an exact encoding with
O(log n) rules: E(2k) ::= E(k) E(k) gives "exactly 2^k" per power of two, and
T(k) ::= E(p) T(k - p) | T(p - 1), with p the largest power of two <= k,
gives "at most k". The two alternatives accept disjoint counts, so the grammar
stays unambiguous and the sampler carries at most one extra stack per level.
The cap and the silent unbounding are gone. A maximum below its minimum is a
parse error now instead of an underflowing optional-copy count.

tests: the parser cases that pinned the unbounded rewrite, and the nested
{0,99} case that was refused only because unrolling it would have produced
99^6 rules, now check that the grammar parses to a small rule set;
test-grammar-integration checks the accepted strings at 5000 copies for a
maximum, a minimum and maximum, an exact count, a minimum only, and a group.
test-grammar-parser, test-grammar-integration, test-llama-grammar and
test-json-schema-to-grammar pass.

* server: retry a queued load only when it lost the slot race

The queued-load loop caught every std::exception from load(), logged it as
a lost race and retried without waiting. Only "model limit reached" is that
race (the capacity re-check under the lock after try_claim released it);
"failed to spawn server instance", "model ... is not found" and "failed to
get a port number" are final, and retrying them spun the loop with a warning
per turn until the client gave up.

load() now throws server_models_capacity_error for the race; the loop keeps
retrying that one and lets anything else propagate after re-taking the lock
and returning the turn, so the waiter's own error reaches its client and the
other waiters get their turn.

The compatibility check was unconditionally rejecting GGML_OP_CONCAT and
GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID, but only specific sub-cases actually block graph
capture:

qwen3.6-35B use dim=0 for SSM conv state concatenation.

IDs to host with stream->wait() and cannot be captured. But the fused
single-token decode path in ggml_sycl_mul_mat_id_mmvq_fused() (ne12==1,
FP32 src1) runs ggml_sycl_mul_mat_vec_q_id() entirely on GPU with no
host wait, and is graph-compatible.

with LIFO linear allocation. The src1_q8_alloc temporary in the fused
MUL_MAT_ID path always gets pool_addr+0, making addresses stable across
graph replays when g_ggml_sycl_use_async_mem_op is set.

fix: exclude single-expert MUL_MAT_ID from graph capture

The graph gate's fused_dispatchable predicate didn't rule out src0's
optimized_feature.reorder flag having been set by the *generic*
opt_for_reorder() (a wider type set - Q1_0/Q4_0/Q8_0/Q2_K/Q3_K in
addition to Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K - than the ID-specific reorder dispatcher
ggml_sycl_mul_mat_vec_q_id_reorder(), which only implements
Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K) via a dense MUL_MAT sharing the same extra.

That requires ggml_can_mul_mat()'s t1->ne[2] % t0->ne[2] == 0 to hold
together with should_reorder_tensor()'s src1->ne[2] == 1, which is only
satisfiable when t0->ne[2] (n_expert) == 1 - and reorder_qw() itself
only supports Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K once ne[2] > 1, so a real (n_expert > 1)
multi-expert tensor can never take the wider-type poisoning path in the
first place. Requiring ne[2] > 1 in the gate closes the theoretical
n_expert == 1 edge case for zero runtime cost - a single-expert
MUL_MAT_ID isn't worth graph-capturing anyway - without the false-reject
an unconditional reorder-state check would otherwise impose.

feat(moe-cache): add SYCL expert-cache provider

Adds a SYCL twin of ggml-vulkan-moe-cache.cpp: a MoE expert-cache
provider that keeps the hottest CPU-resident MoE expert weights
resident in VRAM so decode-time expert matvecs run on SYCL instead of
the CPU MUL_MAT_ID path. Registered from ggml_backend_sycl_reg(),
implementing the shared ggml_moe_cache_api contract.

Adapted from sarashin65/llama.cpp-moe-cache's SYCL provider (the only
prior SYCL implementation, built against an older leloch-era API on a
different tree) to this fork's current API
(query_config/query_device/query_shape/query_fused,
session_create(backends, n, config), begin/plan/dispatch/collect/end)
and its shared moe-cache-common.h session/pool/LRU/eviction
infrastructure, following the Vulkan provider's proven v1 shape
(synchronous fills, one pool per expert shape/type, no fused SwiGLU).

Reuses existing infrastructure rather than porting sarashin's from-
scratch SYCL kernels:
- dispatch() calls the existing ggml_sycl_mul_mat_vec_q_id() dispatcher
  (mmvq.cpp) directly - the cache slab is addressed exactly like the
  stacked expert-weight buffer that function already expects, with
  pool slot indices standing in for expert ids and expert_size as the
  inter-expert stride; each hit row carries its own activation via a
  nonzero src1_row_stride, the same mechanism the real MoE routing path
  uses for its ne11>1 case.
- slabs and scratch buffers are plain sycl::malloc_device USM
  allocations. Unlike Vulkan, SYCL needs no staging buffer or
  UMA/discrete distinction: queue::memcpy moves data between host and
  device directly regardless of topology, and there is no
  pipeline/shader compilation step since the kernel is already built
  into libggml-sycl.so.
- activation quantization is a host-side scalar Q8_1 quantizer (copied
  from the Vulkan provider's approach - rows are few and small, not a
  hot path), uploaded to a device scratch buffer before dispatch.

The wtype-dispatchability check is a local copy of
ggml_sycl_mul_mat_vec_q_id()'s switch rather than a shared predicate,
to avoid a duplicate-symbol collision with PR #58 (which adds the
equivalent shared predicate to mmvq.hpp/mmvq.cpp on a separate,
not-yet-merged branch).
