fix: address PR #61 review findings (LRU corruption, UAF, budget, floors)

Sourcery:
- dispatch(): (size_t)node->pool_index >= 0 is always true after the
  unsigned cast, so a negative pool_index silently fell through to
  pool_slabs[0] instead of being rejected. Check the signed value first.
  (Also present verbatim in ggml-vulkan-moe-cache.cpp; not touched here.)

gemini-code-assist:
- dispatch(): a malloc_device throw right after free left d_ids/d_act/
  d_out pointing at already-freed memory with a stale nonzero _cap, so
  a later smaller request could skip reallocation and use-after-free.
  Reset pointer+cap to null/0 immediately after freeing.
- find_or_create_pool(): reserve pools/pool_slabs capacity before the
  slab allocation so the two push_backs after it cannot throw and
  desync these parallel vectors; moved the allocated_bytes increment
  to after both succeed (strong exception guarantee).
- moe_cache_device (shared header) had no virtual destructor despite
  being held as unique_ptr<moe_cache_device> and holding a derived
  moe_cache_sycl_device via that base pointer - real UB, silently
  skipping ~moe_cache_sycl_device() (leaking its USM buffers) rather
  than crashing. This also affects the already-merged Vulkan provider
  identically; fixed at the shared base rather than patched around
  per-provider.
- dispatch(): null-check each act_rows[i] before dereferencing, since
  this is called through a public C API function-pointer table, not an
  internal invariant - matches collect()'s existing dst_rows[i] check.

chatgpt-codex-connector:
- find_or_create_pool(): each new (expert_size, wtype) pool drew from
  the full configured per-device budget again instead of what's left
  after earlier pools, so multiple expert shapes could each claim the
  entire cap. Pass the remaining budget (fixed independently of
  Vulkan, which has the same gap but wasn't touched here).
- plan(): a duplicate expert within one plan() call (a routed batch
  commonly repeats a popular expert across tokens) hit pool.map.emplace
  silently failing on the second occurrence, leaking a second copied-
  and-promoted slot that was never reachable from pool.map again.
  Coalesce: ride along on the pending fill instead of allocating a
  second slot for the same key.
    - This introduced its own regression, caught by re-running the
      real end-to-end model test after the fix: promoting two pending
      entries that share a slot called moe_cache_lru_push_back on that
      slot twice, corrupting the LRU list with a self-referencing node
      and producing garbage generation output. Fixed by only
      transitioning state/LRU membership once per slot; every entry
      still gets its own reader/pin.
- dispatch(): the ggml_sycl_mul_mat_vec_q_id() call itself sat outside
  any try/catch; a synchronous SYCL exception from kernel submission
  would have propagated through this C API function pointer into
  ggml-cpu.c (a plain C file) - undefined behavior / terminate. Wrapped
  it with the same catch used for the surrounding memcpy/wait calls.
- invalidate(): range-checked [tensor_base, tensor_base+expert_size)
  regardless of which expert a slot actually cached, so a mutation to
  any expert after index 0 missed its slot (stale weights stay
  resident) while mutating expert 0 dropped every cached expert on the
  tensor. Include the expert offset. (Also present verbatim in
  ggml-vulkan-moe-cache.cpp; not touched here.)
- session_create(): forced/"on" mode carried the generic 1 MiB
  min-expert floor even though query_device() (SYCL has no real
  compute-capability concept, always reports the Ampere-equivalent 800)
  already advertised 512 KiB as cacheable for this device - begin()
  then silently rejected experts that fit/placement already counted as
  cacheable. Resolve the floor from the device capability regardless of
  automatic/forced mode. This is the exact gap the PR's own smoke test
  needed GGML_CUDA_MOE_CACHE_MIN_EXPERT_KB=256 to work around.
- Added the canonical GGML_TYPE_Q1_0 case to both
  ggml_sycl_mul_mat_vec_q_id() (mmvq.cpp - it already has Q1_0 support
  in the non-ID MMVQ path, just not the per-expert ID dispatcher) and
  this file's local sycl_moe_wtype_dispatchable() predicate, closing
  the one canonical type that was silently unreachable end-to-end.

Not fixed (deferred, explained in PR review reply): "size pools for
experts across tensors" - the pool's slot count is capped by one
tensor's n_expert even though the pool is shared by design across every
tensor of that (expert_size, wtype). Real, and consistent with this
PR's own high eviction counts, but also present verbatim in the Vulkan
provider; removing the cap outright would trade the current
under-sizing for single-shape budget monopolization (the first pool
created would claim the whole remaining budget). The correct fix -
sizing from the aggregate shape inventory moe_cache_device already
tracks - is a shared pool-sizing design change affecting both
providers, out of scope here.

A second review round traced a real gap: --moe-cache on/auto/soft (no
explicit MiB) reach the provider with budget_mib=0. fit.cpp's own
placement planner separately computes a projected free-VRAM figure to
decide whether to spill routed experts to host RAM, assuming a cache
will absorb the resulting slowdown - but that computed figure is never
wired back into cparams.moe_cache_budget_mib (confirmed by reading
common/fit.cpp, common/common.cpp, and src/llama-context.cpp: the
final ggml_backend_sched_set_moe_cache call always receives the
original, still-zero value). Merging the provider as-is would let
fit's spill decision go through while the actual session stays
dormant (begin() always rejects on budget_mb == 0) - a real decode
regression for anyone following the documented `--fit on --moe-cache
auto` usage pattern with a model that needs spilling. This same gap
already affects the Vulkan provider identically; it's just never been
exercised because no SYCL provider existed to trigger the interaction
during review.

Tried and reverted the two API-level fixes considered for this:
- Making sycl_moe_query_config() decline (return 0) for a
  would-be-zero automatic-mode budget: broke the shared
  test-moe-cache.cpp capability-query contract (cache-capabilities),
  which calls query_config with synthetic probe parameters expecting
  default-value responses independent of whether a budget currently
  exists. The real problem is common/fit.cpp's placement decision
  proceeding without checking the resolved budget, not this function's
  contract - fixing it here breaks a use case that has nothing to do
  with the actual bug.
- Growing pools incrementally as new tensors sharing a shape are
  discovered (via the already-present-but-unused
  moe_cache_device.seen_tensors field), to also close the separately
  flagged pool-thrashing gap in the same pass: implemented and it
  built/linked, but broke test-moe-cache's cache-complete-pools case,
  which showed the real problem with a greedy per-discovery growth
  heuristic - it turns pool sizing into a discovery-order race between
  (expert_size, wtype) shapes for a shared budget. A shape whose
  tensors are discovered first can grow to consume most of the budget
  before a later-discovered shape gets a chance, potentially starving
  it below the minimum pool size. The correct fix needs the aggregate
  shape inventory known in advance (or a second pass) to size every
  pool fairly against the whole model's demand at once. Reverted
  rather than ship a heuristic that trades one imbalance for another;
  left as documented debt with the incremental-growth design and why
  it doesn't work explained in sycl_moe_find_or_create_pool's comment,
  since it's the natural next attempt.

What's actually fixed: session_create() now derives its own

sycl: add graph record-once/replay-many, DMMV row-tail guard, FA buffer alloc fix

Port of three upstream ggml-org/llama.cpp SYCL changes onto this fork's
already-diverged graph-capture machinery (PR #58's fused-MUL_MAT_ID gate,
graph_recording RAII guard, dev_ctx failure tracking, graph_profile counters):

- ggml-org/llama.cpp#28725 (Todd Malsbary): SYCL graphs now record once and
  replay across stable-shape calls instead of re-recording and update()-ing
  every token. Adds a per-context map of graphs keyed by first-node pointer
  (multiple graphs per context, needed when compute splits across CPU/GPU via
  --n-cpu-moe), a warmup state machine (2 stable calls before the first
  replay), node/src property diffing to detect when a cached graph is stale,
  and a timeout-based eviction sweep (GGML_SYCL_GRAPH_EVICTION_TIMEOUT,
  default 10s). check_graph_compatibility() gained a ctx parameter and now
  also rejects any node whose ggml_sycl_mul_mat() dispatch reaches a oneMKL
  or oneDNN library GEMM (mul_mat_uses_library_gemm(), mirroring this fork's
  actual dispatch branches including the WHT-hint fwht early-out), plus
  OUT_PROD/CONV_3D/SOLVE_TRI and library-routed FLASH_ATTN_EXT. This fork's
  own CONCAT dim==3 and fused-MUL_MAT_ID checks are kept; graph_needs_reorder()
  is extended to also cover MUL_MAT_ID Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K, which upstream never
  needed since it rejects all MUL_MAT_ID outright.

  Closes a UAF the upstream design doesn't have to worry about: this fork's
  FA K/V F16 scratch (fattn_buffers(), grows in 16 MiB chunks, shared per
  context) can be reallocated while re-recording one graph, while another
  cached graph in the new multi-graph map still holds the old (now-freed)
  pointer baked into its recorded kernel args. ensure_half() now reports
  reallocation via an out-param, and a growth event evicts every other
  cached graph in the context so they fully re-record on their next use.

- ggml-org/llama.cpp#27689: fattn-buffers.cpp used raw sycl::malloc_device/
  sycl::free instead of the shared ggml_sycl_malloc_device/free_device
  helpers, so KV scratch allocations bypassed the Level Zero relaxed
  allocation limits extension and could fail above 4 GiB.

- ggml-org/llama.cpp#29338: guard DMMV against reading past ncols on
  row-tail columns; adds a MUL_MAT_ID_REUSE test-backend-ops case that
  exercises shared quantized weights across decode/batch/decode dispatch
  (16/16 pass on this fork's SYCL backend).

fix: address PR #62 review findings (UAF, stale replay, memcmp, WHT/reorder gates)

Addresses real bugs found by an external code review plus gh-resolve threads
from sourcery-ai, gemini-code-assist, coderabbitai, and chatgpt-codex-connector,
all independently converging on the same root issues:

- FA K/V F16 scratch (fattn_buffers(), shared per SYCL context) can grow and
  free its old allocation via any eager (non-recorded) flash-attention call,
  not just the recording path my original fix covered. A cached graph
  elsewhere in the multi-graph map could then replay with a freed pointer
  baked into its recorded kernel args - a device use-after-free. Replaced the
  "erase every other cached graph when growth is detected during a record"
  mechanism with a generation counter on ggml_sycl_fattn_kv_buffers (bumped
  by ensure_half() on every real reallocation, from any call site). Each
  ggml_sycl_graph now records the generation it was built against and is
  forced to re-record before replay if the context's current generation has
  moved on. Also drops the now-unnecessary bool* growth out-param from
  ensure_half(), closing a separate nitpick about its reset semantics.

- A failed graph re-record left warmup_complete and exec_graph untouched, so
  a later call could replay a stale executable graph recorded against old
  node properties and pointers. Now resets both on failure.

- node_properties compared the entire ggml_tensor struct via memcmp,
  including padding and the tensor name buffer's uninitialized tail bytes -
  theoretically spurious mismatches that would force needless re-recording.
  Redefined it to store only the fields that matter (data pointer, type, op,
  ne, nb, op_params, plus the existing src arrays).

- mul_mat_uses_library_gemm() treated every Hadamard-hint-tagged MUL_MAT as
  never using a library, but ggml_sycl_mul_mat() only takes that early-out
  when ggml_sycl_op_fwht() actually handles the shape; unsupported shapes
  fall through to ordinary dispatch, which can reach oneMKL for F32 rotation
  weights. Added ggml_sycl_fwht_supported_shape() to mirror fwht.cpp's own
  preconditions and only short-circuit when they actually hold.

- graph_needs_reorder()'s MUL_MAT branch didn't gate on src0's type: for
  types reorder_qw() never handles (F16, IQ*, MXFP4, ...) it read as
  "reorder eligible" but could never satisfy optimized_feature.reorder,
  permanently disabling graphs for such models on the pre-2026-toolchain
  compile path (inert on this fork's actual 2026.0 build). Added the same
  ggml_sycl_supports_reorder_mul_mat_sycl() type gate used elsewhere.

- GGML_SYCL_GRAPH_EVICTION_TIMEOUT<=0 broke the eviction-sweep math (the
  sweep runs on every call and evicts the entry just looked up before it is
  used), silently preventing any graph from ever warming up. Clamped to a
  minimum of 10 with a warning at parse time.

- Factored the duplicated direct-execution instrumentation block (two call
  sites) into a shared ggml_sycl_graph_direct_compute() helper.

- Updated CLAUDE.md: the prior "SYCL-Graph replay cannot amortize on this
  driver" standing decision described the old per-call re-record-and-update
  design. Superseded with this PR's real measurement (graph_calls=1
  replay_calls=46 on a real decode run); the actual remaining limit is no
  in-place graph update support on DG2 (update_calls=0 always), not an
  inability to amortize via replay.

fix: address PR #62 re-review findings (over-alloc, reorder gate, unwind safety)

A second, independent external re-review confirmed the prior round's fixes and
found two incomplete ones plus two new gaps. All addressed here:

- prepare_fattn_buffers sized FA K/V F16 scratch on src type alone, ignoring
  whether the selected kernel variant actually needs an F16 conversion buffer
  at all (need_f16 in fattn-vec.hpp). This over-allocated for native-quant
  decode paths (e.g. q8_0/q8_0 VEC) and, under the new generation-counter
  design, forced an unnecessary re-record of every other cached graph on each
  such allocation. Traced the call graph and warmup state machine: every
  re-record is either preceded by a real eager call with identical node/src
  properties (which already sized the buffers correctly via the real kernel's
  own need_f16 logic), or forced only because another graph's growth bumped
  the shared generation counter - meaning the buffer is already at least as
  large as this graph has ever needed, since ensure_half() never shrinks.
  Removed prepare_fattn_buffers entirely as redundant, and added a before/
  after generation check around the record itself as a backstop: if the
  generation moved during recording anyway (the one case that doesn't call
  the wait() that would otherwise turn into a hard SYCL_CHECK abort - a
  first-ever allocation with no prior buffer to free), the recording is
  discarded as a failure instead of finalized.

- graph_needs_reorder()'s MUL_MAT branch gated eligibility on
  ggml_sycl_supports_reorder_mul_mat_sycl() alone, but opt_for_reorder() (the
  code that actually performs the reorder) dispatches to
  ggml_sycl_supports_reorder_dmmv() or ggml_sycl_supports_reorder_mmvq()
  depending on which path the runtime picks - both broader than the
  mul_mat_sycl predicate for K-quants. Using only the narrowest predicate
  could judge a node "no reorder needed" while a reorder actually happens
  during capture, the hang this gate exists to prevent (inert on this fork's
  2026.0 build, live on the pre-2026-toolchain path the gate targets). Now
  unions all three predicates.

- The submit/wait catch block (a graph launch or wait() throwing) left
  warmup_complete and exec_graph untouched, same bug class as the
  already-fixed record-failure path but for this call site
  (chatgpt-codex-connector). Now resets both there too.

- Recording was not unwind-safe: the RAII guard reset the graph_recording
  flag but never called end_recording() itself, so an exception thrown out of
  compute_impl mid-capture would leave the SYCL queue stuck in the recording
  state. Traced the two concretely-named reachable-today hazards: SET_ROWS's
  host-fallback path (unconditional stream->wait() for K-quant/IQ
  block-structured types) is only reached for types that are not valid
  --cache-type-k/-v choices (see kv_cache_types in common/arg.cpp) - added a
  defensive type gate in check_graph_compatibility anyway, since nothing else
  enforces that invariant. Sparse FA (GGML_SYCL_SPARSE_FA=1, opt-in, off by
  default) genuinely can reach a wait() when enabled; exported
  ggml_sycl_flash_attn_ext_sparse_applicable() to gate it the same way
  library-routed nodes are gated. Rewrote the RAII guard itself to call
  end_recording() in its destructor (best-effort, swallowing secondary
  exceptions) unless the success path already called it explicitly.

- Checked the device pool for the same UAF class as the FA-buffer fix: this
  fork never compiles in GGML_SYCL_SUPPORT_VMM, so new_pool_for_device()
  always returns the legacy pool. Its free() only parks pointers for reuse
  and calls the real device free solely in the rare all-256-slots-full case,
  so pool-allocated addresses (src1 q8_1 buffers, dst_tmp, KV_max) are stable
  for the context's lifetime under normal operation - not a live risk here.

- Added a gen_rerecords profile counter (incremented exactly where the
  generation-mismatch check forces a re-record) so the fattn-generation path
  is directly observable rather than inferred.

models : fill the unwritten rollback snapshot slot on short ubatches

Ports ggml-org/llama.cpp#29454 (goodbadwolf, closed unmerged upstream
on 2026-09-27 - see below) onto this fork.

A ubatch with fewer tokens than K, the live state plus n_rs_seq
rollback snapshots, left one snapshot slot unwritten in delta-net,
mamba2, lfm2, and bailingmoe3's own state-write code. Rolling back the
whole ubatch then read that slot, which held whatever was last written
there. The fix copies the state from before the ubatch into that slot,
unconditionally (not just for short ubatches), so the graph shape does
not depend on ubatch length.

test_short_ubatch_rollback is new: it rolls back whole ubatches of
every length from 1 to n_rs_seq, for two sequences at once.

## Adaptation required

delta-net-base.cpp has two state-write code paths this fork added on
top of upstream: the plain path (gdn_replay == false, structurally
identical to upstream's single path) and a fork-only DRC speculative-
decoding replay path (gdn_replay == true, ingr_all != nullptr) that
replays ingredients from a checkpoint rather than storing full state
snapshots - upstream has no equivalent. git apply --3way's context
matching misidentified which occurrence of the "op writes the last
min(n_seq_tokens, K) snapshots" comment to patch, and inserted
upstream's fix into the replay path instead of the plain path.

Applied the fix to the correct (plain) location instead, using the
same base_slot/dst_base pattern upstream provides. Deliberately did
NOT invent an equivalent fix for the replay path: it stores ingredients
to replay forward from a checkpoint, not materialized state snapshots,
so there is no single unwritten "snapshot slot" to fill the same way -
determining whether an analogous gap exists there, and what the correct
fix would be, is new engineering this port does not attempt.

## Verification

Per this fork's evidence rules, ran the ported test on unmodified
master first (should fail) before applying the fix (should pass):
- Unmodified master + ported test: nemotron-h, kimi-k3, lfm2, and
  bailingmoe3 all fail test_short_ubatch_rollback with real (1e-4 to
  4e-3 nmse) mismatches - the bug reproduces as described. dsv4 and
  the base "plain" case do not hit this gap and pass either way.
- This fix + ported test, 3 repeated ctest runs: nemotron-h, dsv4,
  kimi-k3, lfm2, bailingmoe3, and plain all pass consistently (7/8).

## test-recurrent-state-rollback-gdn-replay: pre-existing, unrelated flakiness found

This target fails on every run, but this is NOT caused by this PR.
Isolated with a 2x2 swap of {this fix, master} src against {this
test file, master test file}: gdn-replay fails identically with
EITHER src state, and the reported nmse is different on every
repeated run (8.8e-15, 1.6e-11, 2.1e-11, 2.4e-13 across four runs of
byte-identical unmodified master) - genuine run-to-run nondeterminism,
not a deterministic regression from this change. The failing check
(`replay_and_compare("full")`, nmse_eps = 0.0, a pre-existing
zero-tolerance state save/load replay comparison) is unmodified by
this PR. Root cause not identified; most likely a pre-existing data
race in the 12-thread CPU backend's gdn_replay state computation,
given the extremely small (rounding-noise-scale) and non-reproducible
magnitude. Reported here rather than silently worked around.

sycl: grouped MoE XMX GEMM for IQ weights (port of upstream #29245) (#67)

* sycl: add a grouped MoE XMX GEMM, gathering IQ weights into the tiles

Ports ggml-org/llama.cpp#29245 (cwriter, open upstream as of 2026-09-27).
A MUL_MAT_ID over a MoE layer ran one library GEMM per expert; with 128
experts and 8 active, each is a sliver, so launches dominate and the
XMX units idle. This groups every expert of a node into one launch,
laying out the work-groups on the host from the row offsets it already
has. Weights are dequantized inside the GEMM, gathered into the XMX A
tiles instead of being written out to f16 and read back; activations
are packed once into VNNI f16.

Nine weight formats have an A stage: iq4_nl, iq3_s, iq4_xs, iq3_xxs,
iq2_xxs, iq2_xs, iq2_s, iq1_s, iq1_m. GGML_SYCL_XMX_GATHER_TYPES
selects them as a bitmask, one bit per format, all set by default; 0
disables the paths (library GEMM baseline). Both paths compute in f16
on XMX, applying to the grouped MUL_MAT_ID path and to plain MUL_MAT
when built with GGML_SYCL_F16=ON.

* common: draft vocab rule, M-RoPE-aware mirroring, deferred rows kept on failure, DFlash block fit

Fifth review pass on the draft error path:

- Vocab: spec_check_draft_ctx() gains a need_vocab rule, used by EAGLE3 and MTP: the draft vocab
  must cover the target's, otherwise init fails with a clear message. EAGLE3 decodes target token
  ids in process(), so a target id past its vocab failed the request (and, through the server's
  decode error path, every concurrent request). The EAGLE3 and DFlash converters take the
  tokenizer from --target-model-dir but pad it to the draft config's own vocab_size, so a smaller
  draft vocab means a misconverted or differently padded draft; MTP runs on the target's model.
  DFlash gets no vocab rule: its process() injects features only and a rejected seed in draft()
  skips the round. draft-simple keeps its per-sequence handling (a vocab gap it tolerates is the
  configuration the rejection repro uses).
- draft-simple: continues_draft() decides whether rows continue the draft memory the way the
  draft's own batch allocator will judge them: an M-RoPE draft accepts a forward jump (image rows
  advance positions by the grid size), any other draft needs pos == pos_max + 1. The strict rule
  stopped mirroring after the first image on M-RoPE drafts. Rows behind the draft memory (stale
  draft rows) are trimmed with a warning, as MTP already does, and the sequence is skipped if the
  memory cannot be trimmed. The same check gates the seed in draft(). The rejection log no longer
  promises recovery "until its next request": a prompt-cache entry that stores a lagging draft
  memory keeps that prefix undrafted. The rejected-token key resets when a sequence mirrors
  cleanly again.
- MTP: the deferred catch-up rows leave `defer` only once the whole batch (catch-up plus seed or
  chain rows) has been built, in flush_deferred(), the chain path and the generic draft path; on a
  rejected row nothing is decoded and the rows stay deferred.
- DFlash: draft() decodes one noise block per drafting sequence in a single batch, so n_max is
  clamped (with a warning) until n_seq blocks fit the draft n_batch, and init fails if not even
  one row per block fits.
- The draft context is created with n_batch >= the target's: llama_context raises the target's
  n_batch to n_rs_seq + 2 for recurrent rollback while the draft context uses n_rs_seq = 0, and
  process() hands the draft whole target batches.
- common_context_can_seq_rm() logs "could not build the probe batch" instead of reporting a
  llama_process() failure that never happened.

sycl: build as ExternalProject for mixed-compiler builds (port of upstream #29506) (#70)

* sycl: use ExternalProject to let this backend be built with SYCL compiler while everything else could use another

Ports ggml-org/llama.cpp#29506 (a1batross, open upstream as of
2026-09-27) onto this fork. Adds an opt-in GGML_SYCL_SEPARATE_BUILD
CMake option (default OFF): when set, ggml-sycl is configured and
built as a nested ExternalProject with its own C++ compiler
(GGML_SYCL_SEPARATE_BUILD_CXX, default icpx), so the top-level project
can use a different compiler for everything else (e.g. GCC or hipcc
for a mixed ROCm+SYCL+Vulkan build) - the same pattern already used
for the hexagon backend. Requires GGML_BACKEND_DL. All GGML_SYCL_*
cache variables are forwarded into the nested build automatically.

Also fixes an existing pre-existing display bug in the log banner:
GGML_SYCL_DNNL is a 0/1 compile define, but the banner checked
"#if defined(GGML_SYCL_DNNL)" (always true once the macro exists, even
when its value is 0), showing "yes" even when oneDNN support was
deliberately disabled. This fork's ggml-sycl.cpp already has the
correct "#if GGML_SYCL_DNNL" form (from a prior resync); this hunk was
a no-op on this tree.

Independent of the opt-in path, one always-active change: sets
CMAKE_LINK_DEPENDS_USE_LINKER OFF for the ggml-sycl target, because
icpx's -fsycl link step generates and deletes temporary objects the
linker depfile then treats as missing, marking ggml-sycl perpetually
out of date and forcing spurious full relinks.

Upstream tested: Ninja, icpx 2026.1, ROCm 7.1 + Vulkan + SYCL in one
tree on an RX 9070 XT + Arc A770 - four devices enumerated
(ROCm0/SYCL0/Vulkan0/Vulkan1), no-change incremental build finished
immediately. Not tested upstream: Windows build; only selected flags
reach the nested build.

feat(ggml): --prefetch-experts-slots - lookahead H2D prefetch of host-resident MoE experts

Ports ggml-org/llama.cpp#28414 (leshchukandrej, draft upstream as of
2026-09-27, blocked mergeable_state) onto this fork.

During prefill the scheduler must upload each expert's weight tensor
from host (or system RAM, via --n-cpu-moe / auto-offload fit margin)
to the GPU right before its MUL_MAT_ID split launches, serializing H2D
behind compute. With large batches every expert is exercised, so
routing ids offer nothing worth waiting for; prefetch instead uploads
full expert tensors through a second backend instance on the same
device into rotating staging slots while the current split computes
(1-deep lookahead), then the consuming split does a per-split
cross-stream event wait that is already satisfied by launch time.

- new flag --prefetch-experts-slots N (default 0 = off; >=2 = full-
  tensor prefetch with 1-deep lookahead; recommended 3; capped at 4)
- GPU staging cost = slots * max expert tensor, lazy-allocated on
  first fire and gracefully disabled if the device lacks async/event
  caps or allocation fails
- decode is unaffected: fires are gated on MUL_MAT_ID splits with
  batch >= 2*n_expert (prefill-scale) and are skipped entirely in
  callback_eval mode
- lossless: prefetch only changes WHEN the bytes land on device - the
  staged copy carries the same host weights and the consuming kernels
  run unchanged after the ready-event wait; with slots = 0 no code
  path changes at all

Backend-agnostic: gated on the generic ggml_backend_dev_props
caps.async/caps.events, not a CUDA-specific check. This fork's SYCL
backend reports both true by default (ggml-sycl.cpp,
ggml_backend_sycl_device_get_props), so the feature is live here, not
inert dead code.

Upstream measured TTFT/prefill speedups on host-expert configs (24B
A3B ncmoe 20: -11% at ~42k-token prompt, -20% at 200 tokens; 21.8GB
35B A3B auto-offload: -22% at ~42k tokens) with flat decode and
unchanged output.

## Adaptation required

Two independent-function false conflicts in ggml-backend.cpp and
llama-context.cpp: this fork's own moe_cache feature (PR #61,
ggml_backend_sched_set_moe_cache) and upstream's new
ggml_backend_sched_set_prefetch_experts_slots both insert at the same
point (right after ggml_backend_sched_new/ggml_backend_sched_create),
so git's 3-way merge treated them as alternatives. Kept both calls;
they configure independent scheduler features.

A third conflict in llama_context_default_params()'s designated-
initializer-style struct literal: upstream's diff still references
this struct's pre-rename field names (.sampler/.n_sampler, singular).
This fork already renamed them to .samplers/.n_samplers (plural,
include/llama.h:441-442) before this port. Added
.prefetch_experts_slots in its correct declaration-order position
(between kv_unified and samplers) using the fork's current field
names, not upstream's stale ones.

Two non-ASCII em dashes in code comments (AGENTS.md: ASCII only)
replaced with '-'.

fix: address PR #72 second-round review (device switch, SYCL gate, staging clears)

- Device switch: prefetch_init() tore down every prefetch resource and rebuilt
  them when a later split targeted a different device. That freed the slot and
  event of any still-pending lookahead entry primed for an earlier split (a
  dangling pointer once that split ran), and its synchronize only covered the
  new device's backend, so a slot the old device's compute was still reading
  could be freed under it. Fixed at the root: never switch devices within one
  scheduler. prefetch_init() now declines for any device other than the one
  prefetch first committed to, and those splits use the ordinary copy path.
  Removes the teardown thrash for alternating devices as well.
- SYCL: a second ggml_backend_sycl_context on the same device shares the
  device's single in-order default queue (dpct default_queue() is a per-device
  singleton), so the prefetch upload cannot overlap the split's compute while
  still paying for a full-tensor upload instead of the routed-experts-only
  copy. Gated SYCL out (with a one-time warning) rather than adding an
  independent queue: this makes --prefetch-experts-slots inert on SYCL.
- Slot zeroing used a host memset on ggml_backend_buffer_get_base(), which is
  not host-dereferenceable for device-local buffers (SYCL, and Vulkan on
  discrete GPUs). Now goes through ggml_backend_buffer_clear().
- Stale padding on slot reuse: the one-time zero at allocation cannot cover a
  smaller tensor later reusing a slot that held a larger one, leaving stale
  bytes where the consuming kernel's alignment over-read lands. Added a shared
  ggml_backend_sched_prefetch_stage() used by both call sites that re-clears
  the slot when the incoming tensor is smaller than what was last staged, after
  a host-blocking event_synchronize on the slot's free event (the caller's
  event_wait is queue-side and does not stop a host-side clear racing the
  previous consumer's kernels).
- Debug log line when a tensor is staged, so a run can show prefetch fired.

  stream. SYCL and Vulkan both share one queue per device, so without the

sycl: link the separate-build module with the install RPATH when one is set

The nested ggml-sycl module is copied into the outer tree and installed
with install(PROGRAMS), so CMake never relinks it with the install
RPATH. Forwarding CMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH alone (#70) therefore did nothing

comes after the forwarded variables, so it applies even if
CMAKE_BUILD_WITH_INSTALL_RPATH was passed as OFF: the nested module has
no separate install copy for that setting to protect.

server: warn when credentials are set through ignored environment variables (#85)

Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) MTP head support, made correct and measurable.

Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) MTP head support, made correct and measurable.

Model and graph
- The MTP graph uses the head's own blk.N.nextn.hc_head_* mixer. All three
  mixer tensors are required when MTP weights are loaded.
- Head-only files run as MTP contexts and as ordinary contexts. A file with
  an incomplete trunk is rejected instead of being run as a head.
- Table-less heads borrow token_embd and output from the target context.
  Borrowed tables are checked for shape and for a buffer type the head's
  devices can use.
- The target leaves its own MTP block unloaded next to a separate head.

Chained drafting (--spec-chain)
- One decode drafts several tokens with the same greedy tokens and top-10
  confidence as sequential drafting; a regression test compares the two.
- Chain decodes validate their batch (a hidden state on every row, no null
  token, no backend sampler, no embeddings mode), keep the catch-up rows
  when a chain decode fails, and grow their reservation in doublings.

Fitting and context
- Adaptive MTP fits with an MTP context for separate-head and shared-model
  setups, and logs why an extra model is measured next to its parent.
- Buffers are planned again when the hidden-state export is switched, and
  embeddings are exported at the context's output width.
- An MTP context also reserves its full ubatch without an output row. The
  allocator packs that catch-up graph worse than the one-output graph, so
  the first catch-up after a draft reallocated 11 MiB that --fit had not
  counted.

State and server
- On-device sequence restore sizes its views in elements, which fixes
  block-quantized K/V types.
- Speculative checkpoints stay on the device only while the device has
  room. The decision is taken at every checkpoint update from the size of
  the copy and the fit margin of that device.
- Tokens accepted from a draft carry the target's probabilities when
  n_probs is requested, ported from upstream llama.cpp PR 27196 with its
  regression test (post_sampling_probs still gets an empty list).
- Every drafter takes its sampler's top-k, CPU and backend, from one
  constant, LLAMA_DRAFT_TOP_K.

Tooling and docs
- scripts/perf/bench_spec.py gains a paired two-build A/B mode with
  fail-closed gates (sole tenancy, GPU fault lines of either driver,
  launch validation including the warmup, an even launch count for the
  ABBA order, the target's argmax on every response row, distinct arm
  names, a known kernel driver), hashes and an ldd manifest of the
  libraries each arm loads, the kernel driver of the render node, and a
  summary that states what a run did not hash or verify, including
  paired cells whose arms generated different token streams.
- speculative-simple checks its prompt decode and accepts a one-token
  prompt.
- docs/speculative.md, docs/KV-cache-quantization.md, two dated research
  notes with the measurements and their limits, four software-stack
  research notes kept as unverified reference, and a review of the xe
  kernel driver against i915 in AGENTS.md.

whole KV cache on the F16 branch we ship (fattn-vec.hpp:170), and the causal
mask is materialised in full (llama-graph.cpp:30).

that understates depth measurements, minimum-of-free-memory sampling, and
the memory-only-floor ceiling analysis that would settle the dequant-bound
claim with a number instead of a mechanism.

P10 is not the port the survey implies. Kmic-68 stops mid-draft on a running
probability product; our MTP drafter commits to a width up front at
speculative.cpp:2285 and has no per-token stop, so the plan adds a stop rule

Thirteen Sourcery findings, all verified against the source before adopting.
Two of them correct claims this set got wrong.

P10 rested on a false premise. I wrote that the MTP drafter "never inspects a
probability mid-draft". It does: speculative.cpp:2363 stops on
cur_p->data[0].p < params.p_min in the non-chained loop, and :2221 stops on
p < params.p_min in the chained one. My earlier grep for those was broken, so I
trusted an empty result. The chained path fuses the decode into one graph but
still runs a host-side selection loop over the packed rows at :2213-2229, so
chain mode is in scope after all. p_cum is a plain additional stop condition, and
P10 is now marked a port rather than a decoupling.

P12 has two holes. fill_mask writes -abs(p0 - p1) when hparams.use_alibi, so the
tensor carries a bias a visible-cell count cannot express, and it only masks
future tokens under cparams.causal_attn, so a prefix representation would hide
cells a noncausal attention is meant to see. Both now force the full tensor.

P06's parity requirement was the wrong invariant: it asked the new rule to match
the greedy rule, which already reproduces the target distribution, so a sampler
preserving neither would pass. It now has to reproduce p, the acceptance evidence
is a stated chi-square and total-variation test at 100000 draws, the fallback is
named as exact-match rather than greedy, and R06.1a requires the recorded
distributions to move in lockstep with the token vector through checkpoint
replay so a token is never verified against another token's q.

P07's keep recurrence clamped the product rather than the ratio, letting keep
rise after a position failed. That is Kmic-68's form and it is wrong for a prefix
survival probability; R07.2a says so explicitly so the port does not copy it.

P05 required an ascending-id tie-break the existing path does not provide:
partial_sort_inplace compares logit only and std::partial_sort is not stable. The
prefilter now falls back on a tie at the k-th position.

Also: P10 declares P01, its baseline; P04 records carry a request identifier so
slot reuse cannot merge cycles; and the README regression floor says 75/50 CPU,
which is what the research note records on the final source, not the 77/51 I
measured before the PR 90 squash.

The thirteen Gemini threads ask for commit-pinned blob URLs on every citation.
Declined, with the base commit now stated once in the README instead.

* docs(plans): address the second review pass

Twelve findings from chatgpt-codex-connector, each verified before adopting.
Two correct claims of mine, one exposes a hole in P12, and one contradicts the
previous review on P07.

P12's premise does not hold for our cache. Kmic-68 argue that for one sequence
in position order, query t sees exactly the first L0+t cells.
set_input_kq_mask_impl at llama-kv-cache.cpp:2258-2281 builds an index list
instead: it tests cells.is_empty, cells.seq_has and cells.pos_get per cell and
pushes survivors. Deletion, reuse and shifting leave holes, so visible cells need
not occupy [0, L) and a prefix length would attend to invalid cells and miss
valid ones. R12.0a makes proving compactness an explicit precondition, and the
plan now says the premise is ours to establish rather than theirs.

P12 also needs cparams.flash_attn in its eligibility. The non-FA path at
llama-graph.cpp:2809-2844 routes through ggml_soft_max_ext with a complete mask
and consumes no prefix lengths, so a single-sequence non-FA decode would have
lost its causal mask.

P07: two reviewers proposed different recurrences for keep. One says clamp the
ratio so keep is non-increasing; the other says track the unclipped cumulative
product and clamp that, because consecutive ratios of 2 then 0.5 give keep = 0.5
under the clipped-product form where the prefix is acceptable with certainty. I
am not adjudicating a theorem from memory. R07.2 states the definition, R07.2a
rejects the clipped-product form and records that Kmic-68 ships it, and R07.2b
requires the choice to be validated against Algorithm 2, since R07.4's gain
figure is only meaningful under the correct one.

Also: P10 cited :2404 as the stop site when it is the draft_add failure path,
the p_min check being :2362-2367. P09's fixed width must be n_max + 1, because
the verify batch carries the previously sampled token and the acceptor asserts
idxs.size() == draft.size() + 1. P09 also needs its own target graph
build-or-reuse counter; P04 profiles the drafter, not the graph P09 changes. P08
cited llama-bench, which has no speculative path and would return identical
numbers whether or not the cap works. P03 gained requirements against the
compiler deleting the loads that define its floor. P01's bench_spec citation
moved to :306 in the squash. The README now records the Kmic-68 branch tip
separately from the merge base, and 26 tests rather than 25.

* docs(plans): third review pass, and P07's recurrence was wrong

Seventeen findings: six CodeRabbit, seven codex-connector, four Copilot.
Every substantive one verified against the source before adopting.

P07 was wrong and I have the paper to settle it. Two reviewers said Algorithm 2
specifies the clipped product; one of them cited the line. It does:

  p_i = min{ p_{i-1} * M_b(X_i | c, X^{i-1}) / M_s(X_i | c, X^{i-1}), 1 }

which is Algorithm 2 line 4. So p_i is non-increasing, Kmic-68's shipped form is
the correct one, and my previous commit, which rejected it in R07.2a on the
grounds that keep must not rise, had it backwards. R07.2 now states the
clipped recurrence, R07.2a rejects the unclipped-cumulative variant instead,
R07.2b points the accept test at the algorithm's h_i^block and the residual at
p_res^block, and R07.4 no longer claims the block and per-token figures share a
recurrence, because they do not and were never meant to. The file also records
that an earlier revision had it backwards. Leaving this unsettled rather than
adjudicating from memory was the right call; settling it the wrong way was not.

P11 was scoped too narrowly. fattn-tile.hpp declares a sycl::half2 VKQ at :781
and a sycl::float2 VKQ at :799, selected by SYCL_FAST_FP16, which common.hpp:52
defines unconditionally with a comment saying removing it breaks the file. So
TILE accumulates in fp16 across the KV cache even in the default FP32 build, and
R11.3's "fp32 path unchanged" exemption applied only to VEC. R11.3a folds TILE
too, and the acceptance now tests TILE with the flag both on and off.

P08's cap is silently undone below a floor: llama-context.cpp:390-402 raises
n_batch and n_ubatch to n_rs_seq + 2 with only a warning, and common.cpp:1308
zeroes the fit context's n_rs_seq, so fit would report a smaller buffer than the
runtime reserves. R08.4a and R08.4b fix both.

P05's guard was insufficient twice over. common_sampler_init at sampling.cpp:325
merges the model's suppress tokens into a logit-bias sampler ahead of TOP_K
unconditionally, so a draft GGUF carrying tokenizer.ggml.suppress_tokens has a
bias even when the speculative params set none. And a tie anywhere inside the
retained top-k can reorder candidates under an identical draw, not only a tie at
the boundary.

Also: P12 needs the graph-reuse predicate to re-check compactness, since
llm_graph_input_attn_kv::can_reuse checks dimensions only, and a backend
capability gate, since GGML_OP_FLASH_ATTN_EXT is implemented by CPU, Vulkan,
OpenVINO and SYCL here. P09 must not let padded rows reach a speculative
implementation, because the server passes batch.view unchanged and each one
mirrors that batch into the draft context. P04 must use the replay-adjusted
accepted count. P06 must draw from the top-p-truncated distribution rather than
truncating the recorded copy afterwards, which would leave q(x) = 0.

* sycl: compile out the XMX gather GEMMs for DG2 AOT builds (GGML_SYCL_XMX_GATHER)

The XMX gather GEMMs from PR #67 (fused-gemm.cpp) use a sub-group-16
8x16x16 fp16 joint_matrix shape. DG2 does not report it, so the runtime
gate never selects them on the A770. JIT builds are unaffected, because a
kernel is compiled only on first launch. An AOT build with
GGML_SYCL_DEVICE_ARCH=acm-g10 compiles every kernel at link time, and IGC
2.41.5 crashes on these:

  [acm-g10] IGC: Internal Compiler Error: Floating point exception
  icpx: error: gen compiler command failed with exit code 245

The Arch package worked around this with a local patch and
-DGGML_SYCL_NO_XMX_GATHER in CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS. Move the fix into the tree:

- New CMake option GGML_SYCL_XMX_GATHER (default ON). The kernels are
  compiled out automatically when GGML_SYCL_DEVICE_ARCH has an entry
  starting with acm, dg2, xe-hpg or IP 12.55-12.57 (for every target in
  the list), and always when the option is OFF. CMake prints which case
  applied.
- Compiled out defines GGML_SYCL_NO_XMX_GATHER (the packager's name, so
  their flag stays harmless). fused-gemm.cpp then keeps only stubs that
  return false, including the capability check. The startup log prints
  "XMX gather GEMMs disabled by compile flag".
- Documented in docs/backend/SYCL.md (build table row, a dedicated
  section, and a note on the runtime GGML_SYCL_XMX_GATHER_TYPES row), in
  CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and sycl-build-runtime-pins.md, plus a dated
  evidence note, docs/research/sycl-xmx-gather-dg2-aot-2026-09-28.md.

* fix(server): keep speculative checkpoints on the device only with room

The server asked for LLAMA_STATE_SEQ_FLAGS_ON_DEVICE at all six
speculative checkpoint calls. The device copy is allocated at the first
checkpoint, after --fit has placed the model, and it is not part of what
--fit measures. On a device that --fit filled up to its margin the copy
eats into that margin unannounced, and a failed allocation aborts.

common_speculative_checkpoint_flags() compares the size of the copy with
the free memory of every device of the model and chooses the device only
while each keeps its --fit-target margin. Otherwise the checkpoint stays
on the host, as before the on-device change. The server picks the flags
per slot and context at the first checkpoint and keeps them, because an
update and the load that follows have to agree.

Arc A770, Qwen3.5-9B self-draft, one launch per arm, no timing claim:
with the default margin both contexts keep their 50.2 MiB checkpoints on
the device; with --fit off --fit-target 15000 both fall back to the host
(5665.7 and 5665.4 MiB free). Restores happened in both runs and the
kernel log gained no fault line. Summaries are in scripts/perf/results.

The check is made once, at the first checkpoint. Memory taken later by
this or another process is not seen, and the per-sequence copy is still
never freed. The research note records both limits, and corrects its
checkpoint size: 100.5 MiB was the sum over both contexts.

* fix(server): place speculative checkpoints at every update

The device-margin guard chose host or device once per slot and context,
at the first checkpoint. That holds for a state of constant size, such
as the recurrent state of a plain hybrid memory. Where the partial state
includes attention cells (a sliding-window cache under a hybrid memory,
the DeepSeek-V4 raw window) the checkpoint grows with the sequence, and
the state writer allocates a larger device copy on every change of size
without the margin being looked at again.

common_speculative_checkpoint_flags() now takes the placement state of
the sequence and is called before every checkpoint update. The context
still holds the copy of its latest device checkpoint and the writer
frees that before it allocates another, so only the growth over that
copy is compared with the free memory and the --fit-target margin. A
checkpoint that is no larger keeps the device without a memory query. A
load reuses the flags of the update before it.

test_checkpoint_placement covers the three outcomes on the fixture, whose
head context saves its whole cache. Its host branch needs a device that
reports memory, so it runs under --backend SYCL0; with the first
decision kept, as before, it fails there.

Arc A770, Qwen3.5-9B self-draft, one launch per case, no timing claim:
device with the default margin, host with --fit off --fit-target 15000,
restores in both, each decision logged once, no fault line in the kernel
log. No model with a growing partial state was run; the note says so.

* fix(qwen4exp): reserve the catch-up graph of an MTP context

A draft context reserved its full ubatch with one output row only. The
catch-up rows of a draft are decoded without an output row, and the
allocator does not plan that graph as a subset of the reserved one: the
scheduler's device copy of the output indices is empty, the two free
blocks it kept apart merge, and best fit places the tensors above them
differently. On the real Q8_0 head the first catch-up ubatch planned
after a draft needed 152.0078 MiB where 141.0157 MiB were reserved, so
the buffer was reallocated at run time and --fit had not counted the
difference.

Reserve that shape as well for Qwen4Exp MTP contexts, and take the
larger size per backend when a fit only measures. graph_reserve accepts
a graph without output rows for MTP contexts.

The reservation is still 8192 bytes short of what a decode plans
(152.0000 against 152.0078 MiB): the reserved graph carries the mask of
a full cache, a decode a smaller one, and one 8 KiB tensor then lands
above the residual instead of in a hole. Best fit gives no bound there.

test_catchup_reservation checks that the reservation is made. The
fixtures cannot show the growth, it needs the real tensor sizes and a
device, so --catchup-real-head <gguf> runs the decode sequence on a
real head. It failed before this change on the A770 (148.5236 to
152.0078 MiB) and allows the 8 KiB above.

perf(sched): skip the host sync before stream-ordered split input copies (port of Andrei-Dr 0018/0020) (#84)

* perf(sched): skip the host sync before stream-ordered split input copies (port of Andrei-Dr 0018/0020)

When a host-buffer split input (e.g. CPU-computed MoE expert output) is
copied to a SYCL split, the scheduler used to drain the device, then do a
blocking copy that drains it again. A copy enqueued with set_tensor_async
on the split backend's own in-order stream is already ordered after every
earlier read of the destination, so it is now one async enqueue.
GGML_SCHED_COPY_SYNC=1 restores the old waits.

- Only for backends that export the new proc-address hook
  "ggml_backend_async_is_stream_ordered" and use their default buffer
  type in the scheduler. SYCL exports it: every SYCL op, buffer call,
  host allocation and the MoE cache use the device's one in-order default
  queue. Vulkan/OpenVINO keep the synchronize (their write-after-read
  ordering is not audited).
- Host-source lifetime guard, a fork addition. The device reads the host
  source when the copy executes. A backend that got such a copy from a
  non-WEIGHTS host tensor is flagged. Flagged backends are synchronized
  before any host split starts, and after every compute_splits whatever
  its status. This covers two cases the patches' argument misses: a host
  split with only user inputs, and the next graph's set_inputs writing
  into memory an intermediate reused.
- Counters (stream-ordered copies, flushes at host split / graph end)
  are logged at GGML_LOG_DEBUG when the scheduler is freed.
- Docs: GGML_SCHED_COPY_SYNC row in docs/backend/SYCL.md, dev log
  docs/research/sched-stream-ordered-copies-2026-09-28.md.

Built (JIT SYCL, rc 0). Runtime verification pending: the GPU is

openvino: validate REPEAT shapes and cover dynamic multipliers (#96)

* openvino: do not call to_shape() on a dynamic shape in REPEAT

translate_repeat calls to_shape() on both the input and output PartialShape.
to_shape() throws ov::Exception on a dimension that is not static, and the token
axis is dynamic in dynamic or stateful mode, so translating a REPEAT there
aborts the load instead of raising a conversion error the caller could report.

Read the PartialShape and skip any axis whose extent is not known. A repeat is
an integer expansion, so 1 is the only factor that is always valid for an axis
that cannot be tiled yet, and it leaves the initialiser correct for the axes
that can. Rank is still checked, because with a dynamic rank there is no way to
know which axis is which.

Follows the existing pattern in cpy.cpp: rank().is_static() then dim.is_static()
with get_length(). The divisibility check now names the axis instead of
printing the shapes, since a PartialShape has no streaming form.

Found by the review on the (now closed) upstream sync PR #82, which imported
this code from upstream. Master has carried it since the 2026-08-16 sync.

* openvino: derive the REPEAT factor on the dynamic axis at runtime

The previous commit's premise was wrong: the decoder builds both shapes
from the captured ggml extents, so they are always static rank 4 and the
skip it added for a dynamic axis never ran. Drop it, read the shapes with
to_shape() again and restore the shape-bearing error message.

The real hazard is on the axis get_op_dynamic_dim() reports in a dynamic
model, whose captured extent is stale. REPEAT keeps src[0]'s dynamic dim,
so a factor of 1 there tracks the input at any extent and stays constant.
Any other factor means the template is fixed on that axis, so compute it
as template extent / runtime input extent (ShapeOf + Gather + Divide).

Also check the rank explicitly instead of indexing four axes blind.

* fix(server): keep speculative checkpoints on the device only with room

The server asked for LLAMA_STATE_SEQ_FLAGS_ON_DEVICE at all six
speculative checkpoint calls. The device copy is allocated at the first
checkpoint, after --fit has placed the model, and it is not part of what
--fit measures. On a device that --fit filled up to its margin the copy
eats into that margin unannounced, and a failed allocation aborts.

common_speculative_checkpoint_flags() compares the size of the copy with
the free memory of every device of the model and chooses the device only
while each keeps its --fit-target margin. Otherwise the checkpoint stays
on the host, as before the on-device change. The server picks the flags
per slot and context at the first checkpoint and keeps them, because an
update and the load that follows have to agree.

Arc A770, Qwen3.5-9B self-draft, one launch per arm, no timing claim:
with the default margin both contexts keep their 50.2 MiB checkpoints on
the device; with --fit off --fit-target 15000 both fall back to the host
(5665.7 and 5665.4 MiB free). Restores happened in both runs and the
kernel log gained no fault line. Summaries are in scripts/perf/results.

The check is made once, at the first checkpoint. Memory taken later by
this or another process is not seen, and the per-sequence copy is still
never freed. The research note records both limits, and corrects its
checkpoint size: 100.5 MiB was the sum over both contexts.

* fix(server): place speculative checkpoints at every update

The device-margin guard chose host or device once per slot and context,
at the first checkpoint. That holds for a state of constant size, such
as the recurrent state of a plain hybrid memory. Where the partial state
includes attention cells (a sliding-window cache under a hybrid memory,
the DeepSeek-V4 raw window) the checkpoint grows with the sequence, and
the state writer allocates a larger device copy on every change of size
without the margin being looked at again.

common_speculative_checkpoint_flags() now takes the placement state of
the sequence and is called before every checkpoint update. The context
still holds the copy of its latest device checkpoint and the writer
frees that before it allocates another, so only the growth over that
copy is compared with the free memory and the --fit-target margin. A
checkpoint that is no larger keeps the device without a memory query. A
load reuses the flags of the update before it.

test_checkpoint_placement covers the three outcomes on the fixture, whose
head context saves its whole cache. Its host branch needs a device that
reports memory, so it runs under --backend SYCL0; with the first
decision kept, as before, it fails there.

device with the default margin, host with --fit off --fit-target 15000,
restores in both, each decision logged once, no fault line in the kernel

* fix(qwen4exp): reserve the catch-up graph of an MTP context

A draft context reserved its full ubatch with one output row only. The
catch-up rows of a draft are decoded without an output row, and the
allocator does not plan that graph as a subset of the reserved one: the
scheduler's device copy of the output indices is empty, the two free
blocks it kept apart merge, and best fit places the tensors above them
differently. On the real Q8_0 head the first catch-up ubatch planned
after a draft needed 152.0078 MiB where 141.0157 MiB were reserved, so
the buffer was reallocated at run time and --fit had not counted the
difference.

Reserve that shape as well for Qwen4Exp MTP contexts, and take the
larger size per backend when a fit only measures. graph_reserve accepts
a graph without output rows for MTP contexts.

The reservation is still 8192 bytes short of what a decode plans
(152.0000 against 152.0078 MiB): the reserved graph carries the mask of
a full cache, a decode a smaller one, and one 8 KiB tensor then lands
above the residual instead of in a hole. Best fit gives no bound there.

test_catchup_reservation checks that the reservation is made. The
fixtures cannot show the growth, it needs the real tensor sizes and a
device, so --catchup-real-head <gguf> runs the decode sequence on a
real head. It failed before this change on the A770 (148.5236 to
152.0078 MiB) and allows the 8 KiB above.
